INTRODUCTION

Patient /family care study involves the interaction between the patient and the health team. In this, a patient is selected in the ward with a specific disease. The patient is nursed from day one of admission to the day of discharge and follow ups are made to help maintain good health and ensure continuity of care.
The patient/family care study was conducted on 48 year's old female patient, who for the purpose of confidentiality, will be referred to as Miss L.k. with Hypertension in this study. She was admitted to the Sunyani Municipal Hospital, on 200h August, 2023 and discharged on 25th August, 2023.
I introduced myself to her and her family as a student nurse and sought their permission to use her as a patient for my patient/family care study for which they agreed to.
On admission patient’s vital signs read Temperature -36.2 0C, Pulse – 108bpm, Respiration – 29cpm, Blood Pressure – 192/100 mmHg. She spent six days on admission. The health problems identified were; headache, dizziness, palpitation, general body weakness, joint pain and restlessness. A nursing care plan for each identified problem was made. She was being managed on the following prescribed medical treatment; Tablet Nifedipine 30 mg bd  30 days, Tablet Lisinopril 10mg daily  15days, IV Hydralazine 10mg stat dose, Tablet Bendrofluazide 2.5mg daily  10days, IV Cefuroxime 750mg tid  24hours, Tablet diclofenac 100mg bd  5 days. Data was collected through observation, interviews, and other diagnostic procedures. Health problems were identified and interventions were made with patient and family’s co-operation to achieve set goals. On admission, effective medical and nursing care was rendered to her and was discharged without any complications.
Home visits were also made during admission and after discharge to continue her care. Mrs. L K and her family appreciated the care given to them by the entire health team.
This study is presented in five chapters. Chapter one involves the assessment of patient/family, patient particulars such as developmental history, past and present medical history, patient’s lifestyle and hobbies. Family medical history, socio-economic history, admission of patient, literature review of the disease and validation of data.
Chapter two entails analysis of data, comparison of data with standard causes, clinical manifestation, treatment and complication. It involves patient/family strength, health problems and nursing diagnosis.
Chapter three is the planning of patient/family care plan, it includes the use of care plan which diagnosis, objective criteria, nursing orders, nursing interventions and evaluation.
Chapter four contains implementation of patient/family care plan, summary of preparation of patient for discharge, rehabilitation and follow-up or home visits.
Chapter five deals with evaluation of care rendered to patient/family. Statement of evaluation. Amendment of nursing care plan. Summary of nursing care from admission till discharge

1.3 Patient’s Developmental History
Development is a process that creates growth, progress, positive change or the addition of physical, economic, environmental, social and demographic components.
Growth according , is an increase in size of an organism or any of its parts, as measured in increment of weight or volume or linear dimensions, which occurs as a result of hyperplasia or hypertrophy.
Maturation is the emergence of personal and behavioral characteristics through growth processes.
  On direct questioning according to her mother she was delivered at birth by a traditional birth attendant in the house without any health complications. She could not tell the month she started growing teeth but, she started sitting by the ninth month and could walk at age one. Mrs. L.K had no congenital malformation such as cleft palate, cleft lip or club foot. She was still breastfeeding even at the age of two (2) and could walk at age one. Her mother disclosed to her that, she used herbs, animal fat, bones and “adukromunsuo” to bath her.
She was immunized against the six childhood diseases. She recalled that breast development, wider hips, increase in height, growth of pubic hairs and other secondary sexual characteristics were developed after age 12 and she had her menarche at age 14, because of the farming activities she was involved at the early stage of her life, she could not get the chance to play with her friends that much since she was on the farm most of the times after school hours. She stated that she wanted to attend secondary school after completion of junior high but her parents could not allow her and they wanted her to succeed them. Her weight was not recorded at birth.
According to Erickson’s theory of development (1963), psychological development describes the human life cycle as a series of eight ego developmental stages from birth to death. Each stage presents a psycho-social crisis, the goal of which is to integrate physical, maturation and societal demands. The theory focuses on psycho-social task that are accomplished throughout the life cycle. An unsuccessful resolution leaves the individual emotionally handicapped.
According to Erickson’s theory of development, Mrs. L.K is at Generality versus Stagnation. After people in early adulthood have developed a sense of adolescence, they are ready to share their life with others. However, if other stages have not been successfully resolved, young adults may have trouble developing and maintaining successful relationship with others. Mrs. L.K has accomplished generality by contributing to his family, community, work and society as a whole.

heading: 1.9 LITERATURE REVIEW
text:
1.9 LITERATURE REVIEW

Figure 1: Anatomy of the Heart



The circulatory system is an organ system that permits blood to circulate and transport nutrients (such as amino acids and electrolytes), oxygen, carbon dioxide, hormones, and blood cells to and from the cells in the body to provide nourishment and help in fighting diseases, stabilize temperature and pH, and maintain homeostasis.
Main Features of the Human Circulatory System
A liquid, blood, to transport nutrients, wastes, oxygen and carbon dioxide, and hormones.
Two pumps (in a single heart): one to pump deoxygenated blood to the lungs and the other to pump oxygenated blood to all the other organs and tissues of the body
A system of blood vessels to distribute blood throughout the body
Specialized organs for exchange of materials between the blood and the external environment; for example, organs like the lungs and intestine that add materials to the blood and organs like the lungs and kidneys that remove materials from the blood and deposit them back in the external environment
The Heart and Pulmonary System
The heart is located roughly in the center of the chest cavity. It is covered by a protective membrane, the pericardium.
Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium.
It flows through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. The term tricuspid refers to the three flaps of tissue that make up the valve.
Contraction of the ventricle then closes the tricuspid valve and forces open the pulmonary valve.
Blood flows into the pulmonary artery.
This branches immediately, carrying blood to the right and left lungs.
Here the blood gives up carbon dioxide and takes on a fresh supply of oxygen.
The capillary beds of the lungs are drained by venules that are the tributaries of the pulmonary veins.



Figure 2: The Heart and the Pulmonary System




The above figure shows the human heart, with a schematic view of the pathway of blood through the lungs and internal organs. Oxygenated blood is shown in red; deoxygenated blood in blue. Note that the blood draining the stomach, spleen, and intestines passes through the liver before it is returned to the heart. Here surplus or harmful materials picked up from those organs can be removed before the blood returns to the general circulation.
The Coronary System
From the left atrium,
Blood flows through the mitral valve (also known as the bicuspid valve) into the left ventricle.
Contraction of the ventricle closes the mitral valve and opens the aortic valve at the entrance to the aorta.
The first branches from the aorta occur just beyond the aortic valve still within the heart.
Two openings lead to the right and left coronary arteries, which supply blood to the heart itself. Although the coronary arteries arise within the heart, they pass directly out to the surface of the heart and extend down across it. They supply blood to the network of capillaries that penetrate every portion of the heart.
The capillaries drain into two coronary veins that empty into the right atrium.
Diseases of the Coronary system: Arteriosclerosis and Atherosclerosis
The coronary arteries arise at the point of maximum blood pressure in the circulatory system. Over the course of time, the arterial walls are apt to lose elasticity, which limits the amount of blood that can surge through them and hence limits the supply of oxygen to the heart. This condition is known as arteriosclerosis.
Alternatively, fatty deposits, called plaque, may accumulate on the interior surface of the coronary arteries; this condition is known as atherosclerosis. This is particularly common in people who have high levels of cholesterol in their blood. Plaque deposits reduce the bore of the coronary arteries and thus the amount of blood they can carry. Atherosclerosis (usually along with arteriosclerosis) may limit the blood supply to the heart that during times of stress the heart muscle is so deprived of oxygen that the pain of angina is created. It triggers the formation of a clot causing a coronary thrombosis. This stops the flow of blood through the vessel and the capillary network it supplies causing a heart attack. The portion of the heart muscle deprived of oxygen dies quickly of oxygen starvation. If the area is not too large, the undamaged part of the heart can, in time, compensate for the damage.
Coronary bypass surgery uses segments of leg veins to bypass the clogged portions of the coronary arteries.
The Systemic Circulation
The remainder of the system is known as the systemic circulation. The graphic shows the major arteries (in bright red) and veins (dark red) of the system. Blood from the aorta passes into a branching system of arteries that lead to all parts of the body. It then flows into a system of capillaries where its exchange functions take place.










Figure 3: Human Circulation System

Blood from the capillaries flows into venules which are drained by veins.
Veins draining the upper portion of the body lead to the superior vena cava.
Veins draining the lower part of the body lead to the inferior vena cava.
Both empty into the right atrium.
Definition of Hypertension
Hypertension is defined as a consistent constant elevation of the systolic or diastolic pressure above 140/90 mmHg. It is sustained deviation of blood pressure (BP). In adults, hypertension exists when systolic blood pressure (SBP) is equal to or greater than 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) is equal to or greater than 90mmHg for extended periods of time. The diagnosis of hypertension required that elevated readings be present on at least three occasions during several weeks.
       High blood pressure (HBP) means that the heart is working harder than normal, putting both the heart and the blood vessels under strain. HBP may contribute to myocardial infractions, cerebrovascular accident (CVA), renal failure and atherosclerosis. Hypertension causes no symptoms to motivate a person to seek treatment. When symptoms do occur, they signify either secondary causes of hypertension or effects of sustained elevation of BP on target organs (coronary artery disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease or renal insufficiency).
Incidence of Hypertension
In survey period 2017-2018, the prevalence of age – adjusted hypertension was 45.4% among adults and was higher among men (51.0%) than women (39.7%). Hypertension increased with age: 22.4% (aged 18-39), 54.5 % (40-59) and 74.5% (60 and over).
Types of Hypertensions
Basically, we have two (2) types of hypertensions namely:
Primary / Essential / idiopathic / Familial hypertension.
Secondary hypertension.
Primary / Essential / Idiopathic / Familial hypertension.
This type of hypertension has no known cause and intermittent. It can be benign (chronic) or malignant (accelerated) hypertension. The benign does not post much problem and can be with the individual for between 10 – 20 years with no problem. The malignant one however, has rapid onset and very progressive causing damage to the kidney, heart and other vital organs and can kill within two years.

Aetiology / Causes
The causes of primary hypertension are unknown. However, the following have been identified as risks factors or predisposing factors;
Family history of hypertension.
Chronic stress
Race – common in blacks
Physical activities
Obesity
Sex – common in women than men
Smoking
High intake of sodium and saturated fat.
Frequent ingestion of alcohol
Age – increasing age (50 years and above)
Sedentary lifestyle
Over stimulation with coffee.

Secondary hypertension: This is a type of hypertension with a known cause which can be certain drugs such as steroids, oral contraceptive, pregnancy eclampsia, Cushing syndrome neurologic disorders such as brain tumor, Arteriosclerosis and atherosclerosis, etc.
Causes of Secondary Hypertension
This type of hypertension is caused by the following Disease of the heart
Myocardial infection
Stenosis of cardiac valves
Endocrine Disorders
Diabetes mellitus
Primary hyperaldosteronism
Hyperthyroidism
Cushing syndrome.
Renal Disease
Renal parenchyma disease
Renal tumor
Hydro nephritis
Glomerulonephritis
Iatrogenic Factors
Excessive smoking
Pregnancy
Excessive intake of alcohol
Ingestion of estrogen pills


Predisposing Factors of Primary Hypertension
The cause of primary hypertension is unknown but some risks factors have been identified initiations of the condition. These factors are basically genetic which are non – modifiable and environment which are modifiable.

Genetic / non-modifiable factors: these deals with the genes and they are family history, gender and age.
Family history: individuals whose family has history of high blood pressure, has risk of developing this condition at a younger age.
Gender: K plan (1985) has it that, although high blood pressure increases with age, in both males and females, males are usually prone to it at an earlier age than the females do.
Age: The structural and functional charge in the peripheral vascular system are responsible for the increase in blood pressure that occurs with age related process of atherosclerosis / arteriosclerosis plaques and loss of connective tissue elasticity can predispose the aged to high blood pressure resulting in hypertension



Environmental (modifiable) factors.
Stress profile: stressful situations cause the release of catecholamine and also increase the peripheral resistance lending to high blood presence
Occupation: There are certain occupations which are hypertension prone because of the stress level involved in them. Example includes theatre and emergency nursing.
Socio-economic status: groups of people who are economically deprived have a high incidence of increase blood pressure. The factors account for these includes poor nutrition and habits, low status job; frustrations, depression of hostility.
Nutrition: High blood pressure can result by taking excessive salt, calories and alcohol. It has been discovered that, the body’s normal supply of cholesterol also increases the cholesterol in the blood which forms deposits on the arteries causing hypertension.
Obesity: This is usually associated with high blood pressure. This may be due to the increased blood pressure associated with weight gain.
Excessive smoking: Nicotine is a vasoconstrictor thereby increasing blood pressure.
Physical activities individuals who do vigorous activities increase blood pressure.

Pathophysiology of Primary Hypertension
The pathogenesis of essential hypertension is multifactorial and highly complex. The kidney is both the contributing and the target organ of the hypertensive processes, and the disease involves the interaction of multiple organ systems and numerous mechanisms of independent or interdependent pathways. Factors that play an important role in the pathogenesis of hypertension include genetics, activation of neurohormonal systems such as the sympathetic nervous system and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, obesity, and increased dietary salt intake.
Arterial hypertension is the condition of persistent elevation of systemic blood pressure (BP). BP is the product of cardiac output and total peripheral vascular resistance.
Clinical Manifestation of Hypertension
Patients with hypertension may exhibit or manifest some of the following signs and symptoms:
Elevated blood pressure
Severe headache
Tinnitus
Vertigo
Palpitations
Dizziness
Blurred vision
Chest pain
Shortness of breath
Restlessness
General body weakness
Irritability
Mental confusion.

Diagnosis of Hypertension
Measures used in diagnosing hypertension include:
Physical Examination: this is by clerical manifestation outlined earlier.
Urinalysis: for protein to see if kidneys are involved
Chest X-Ray: to see abnormalities of the heart. Eg: left ventricular hypertrophy
Electrocardiography: to reveal cardiomegaly
Serum blood urea and nitrogen level: to reveal renal failure
Lipid profile/ cholesterol: to see if there is high level of lipid in the body system.
Medical Management / Treatment of Hypertension
Essentials Hypertension has no cure but can be controlled with drugs and modification of diet and life style. Secondary hypertension management involves treatment of the underlined causes and controlling hypertensive effect, two main categories of drugs are used in management or treatment of hypertension namely;
Those acting on the kidney (Diuretics)
Those acting on the heart and blood vessels: Vasodilators, Calcium channel blockers, Beta Blockers, Alpha Blockers, and Angiotensin – converting Enzymes (ACE) inhibitors.

Diuretics: Examples
(i) Hydrochlorothiazide (esidrex)
	(ii) Furosemide (Laxis)
	(iii) Spironolactone (Aldactone)

Vasodilators: Examples
(i) Hydralazine (Apresoline)
            (ii) Minoxidil (Ionisten)
            (iii) Sodium nitroprusside (Nitropress)
            (iv) Fenoldopam mesylate (Corloprim)

Calcium Channel blockers: Examples
Nifedipine (procardia or Adalat)
Verapramil (calm, isoptin)
Amlodipine (morvasc)
             (iv) Nicardipine (Cardene)

Beta Blockers: Examples
(i) Doxacosin (Cardura)
            (ii)Prazosin hydrochloride (Miniprass)

Angiotensin Converting Enzymes (A.C.E) inhibitors Examples:
     (i) Captopril (Capoten)
    (ii) Enalopril (Vasolec)
   (iii) Lisinopril (Priniuil)
   (iv) Ramipril (Atlace)

Nursing Management of Hypertension
The nursing care of the hypertension patient begins with reassurance and explanation of the condition to the patient about the causes, predisposing factors. Prevention and side effects of drugs, knowledge about the condition to allay anxiety, therefore, reducing high blood pressure. The patient should be educated on the following: Rest, Diet, observation, modification of lifestyle, elimination, medication and exercises.

Rest: comfort and rest are particularly enforced in severe hypertension. Rest is very important to hypertensive patients and the amount needed depends on the severity of the condition. Rest reduces the workload of the heart, increases urine output and reduces blood pressure therefore patients should be placed in comfortable position (sitting up or fowler position to aid breathing). Patient must be made to understand the need for rest.
Nutrition: The dietician should be informed of the client’s condition so that he/she comes to plan the menu with the client, taking into consideration the client’s likes and dislikes. The patient should take up to only 9gm of salty diet in a day and the rationale behind low salt diet intake should be explained to the patient. Patient should be told not to add salt to cooked food. Patient’s diet should be rich in roughages which help to bring down blood pressure.

Patient should be restricted in the intake of foods rich in fat and cholesterol, eg. Butter, ice cream, egg yolk and fried foods but he/she should be encouraged to take in unsaturated fat like vegetable and corn oil which reduces cholesterol.
Medications: Antihypertensive drugs should be given to patient regularly for a long period to control the blood pressure and drugs should be administered as prescribed by physician. Patient should be educated on the mode of action of the drug as well as the side effects and report them immediately to the physician and should be assisted to develop a simple convenient schedule to take the medication.
Weight reduction: Patient should be encouraged to reduce weight if he/she is obese by performing regular tolerable exercises, avoid taking snacks between meals and educated on his/her diet.
Observation: Patient’s blood pressure should be checked regularly depending on the severity on the condition. Example: every 2hours, 4hours or 6 hours with the patient being in the same position each time. Accurate intake and output chart should be maintained to check fluid and electrolyte balance and daily weighing to determine excessive weight gain.
Adopt Dash Plan (Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension): Educate client to consume diet rich in fruits, vegetables and low dietary products. Dietary sodium restriction should also be discouraged. Patient should also maintain adequate intake of calcium and magnesium for general health.
Health Education: Patient should be educated on the causes, preventions, treatment or management of complications of hypertension. The nurse should ensure that the patient and his/her family understand the need to comply with the drug regimen and dietary restriction and should be educated on the signs and symptoms or complications that need to be reported as soon as possible. Patient should be educated on measures of weight reduction, measures, low fat consumption, side effects of antihypertensive drugs, regular checkup, etc.
  Complications of hypertension
    If patient is untreated, the following complications can result:
The cardiovascular system
Left ventricular hypertrophy- is enlargement and thickening of the walls of your heart’s main pumping chamber.
Myocardial Infection-A blockage of blood flow to the heart muscles
Congestive heart failure-A chronic condition in which the heart doesn’t pump as well as it should.

The Central Nervous System
Hypertension encephalopathy-is general brain dysfunction due to significantly high blood pressure.
Cerebrovascular or brain attack-is when blood flow to a part of your brain is stopped either by blockage or the rupture of the blood vessel.
Renal System
Renal failure-is a medical condition in which the kidneys are functioning at less than 15% of normal.

Retinal System
Retinopathy: blindness – disease of the retina which results in impairment or loss of vision



Prevention of Hypertension
Primary Prevention
Educate patient on the need for adequate exercise such as brisk – walking.
Low dietary intake of salt and fatty foods should be encouraged
Advise patient on the dangers of smoking and alcoholism
Obese patient should be encouraged to join keep fit clubs if possible.

Secondary prevention
Report signs and symptoms early
Educate hypertensive patients to join societies and groups in the community to retrieve stress or emotional disturbances
Educate patient to monitor blood pressure and record for early detection of hypertension
Advice the patient on the need for rest.
Tertiary prevention
Recommend that people with high blood pressure check and monitor their blood pressure regularly
Educate patient to take in prescribed hypertensive drugs regimen as order

Prognosis
Prognosis of hypertension is good if one seeks early medical attention but may worsen if left unmanaged for a long time.

chapter: Chapter Four: Implementation Of Patient / Family Care Plan
heading: 4.1 Summary of actual nursing care rendered to patient and family
text:
4.1 Summary of actual nursing care rendered to patient and family
The nursing care rendered to Mrs. L.K started from the day of admission which was 20th of, August 2023. The nursing care aimed at ensuring comfort of the patient and to promote recovery without any complications. Patient was admitted into the female`s ward at Sunyani Municipal Hospital, with the diagnosis of hypertension. Patient was welcomed into the ward and offered a seat and was warmly welcome and made comfortable in a simple unoccupied bed. Assessment was done and a number of problems identified in a holistic as well as comprehensive care implemented to resolve patient’s problem.

Day of admission (20th August, 2023)
On Monday 20th August, 2021, patient was admitted at the Female`s Ward at the Sunyani Municipal Hospital by Dr. S. M at 2:40pm with a diagnosis of Hypertension. She came in as an ambulant patient and was not accompanied by her daughter.
On admission, patient complained of headache, dizziness, palpitation, general body weakness, joint pain and restlessness. The patient was warmly welcomed into the ward and a simple bed was made for her to rest on. Patient was reassured of her wellbeing. Patient’s particulars such as name, age, sex, residential address was recorded into the admission and discharge book and daily ward state. Her vital signs were also checked and recorded as follows:
Temperature		=	36.2oC– 36.8 oC
Respiration		=	29 cycles per minute – 27 cycle per minutes
Pulse			=	108 beats per minutes – 100 beats per minutes
Blood pressure	=	192/100 mmHg and it was gradually reducing
The following investigations were requested for him; Full blood count, Blood film for malaria parasites, chest x-ray, fasting Blood glucose and urine routine examination. Injection hydralazine 10mg /ml stat was given.  He was managed on the following medications.
Tablet Nifedipine 30mg bd x30 days.
Tablet Lisinopril 10mg daily x 15 days.
Intravenous Hydralazine 10mg stat dose.
Tablet Bendrofluazide 2.5mg daily x 10days.
Intravenous cefuroxime 750mg tid x 24hours.
Tablet diclofenac 100mg bd x 5days.
The belongings of the patient were kept in the bed side locker. The patient was oriented to the nurses’ station, bathroom, toilet, etc. The patient was introduced to the staff nurses and other patients on the ward.
I introduced myself to the patient, as a final year student at Seikwa Nursing and Midwifery training College and expressed my desire to take her for my care study and she also gave me the opportunity to use her for my care study. I used the opportunity given to me to educate her on the condition and the purpose of the care study as well.  I quickly gathered information on the patient’s condition after establishing rapport by asking her how the condition came about and her life style. Patient and her daughter were therefore reassured, that she was in the hands of competent nurses and health professionals to affirm quick recovery and her stay on the ward is temporal and she will be discharged at the appropriate time but she has to continue with her medication prescribed, take it on time and come back for review on the said date. Later her other relatives were in to visit her and to know how she was doing as well. The relatives were told of visiting hours and doctors-ward-rounds as well as time for medications and meals. Patient was also informed that, in case they needed any assistance, they should inform me.
Patient and relatives were informed that the hospital was only a temporary place and that she will be discharged home as soon as she gets better
On admission, patient complained of headache. Tablet Diclofenac 100mg x 5 days was ordered to be added to her medications. An objective was set and a nursing care plan was drawn together with the patient to help restore her bodily comfort within 30 minutes as evidence by patient verbalizing of being relieved from headache. Patient was encouraged to take warm water in the evening before going to bed. Her bed linen was straightened to make it free from creases and cramps and promote comfort. She was provided with a radio set to serve as a diversional therapy for pain. Patient was reassured and prescribed analgesics and IV hydralazine was administered and comfortable bed was made and number of visitors were restricted and their time of stay reduced. Bp was monitored hourly.
Also, patient complained of dizziness. An objective was set and a nursing care plan drawn to help prevent her from sustaining any injury throughout her stay on the ward. Patient was reassured of speedy recovery. A complete bed rest was ensured. She was also assisted in doing all daily activities. She was nursed on a lower bed and bedside rails raised to prevent her from falls.
Patient also complained of body weakness. An objective was set and a nursing care plan was drawn to help her perform activities of daily living with no assistance. Patient was reassured of speedy recovery. Patient’s items were brought closer to her. A complete bed rest was ensured.
Patient complained of palpitation. An objective was set and a nursing care plan was drawn to help her relieved of her palpitation. Patient was taught relaxation techniques to help reduce stress. Patient was reassured of speedy recovery. A complete bed rest was ensured. Mrs. L.K told me her headache has subsided

First day of admission (21th 	August, 2023)
On the 21th August, 2023, patient woke up as early as 5:45am. Patient could not groom herself so she was assisted to brush her teeth and visit the toilet and took her bath and was served with beverage and bread as breakfast. Routine vital signs were checked and it was recorded as follows:
Temperature		36.20C – 36.5 oC
Pulse rate		80 beats per minute- 85 beats per minutes
Respiration 		22 cycles per minute- 25 cycles per minute
Blood pressure	183/90 mmHg
Her medications were served accordingly and recorded. During ward rounds, the lab results were shown to the doctor and she confirmed that everything was normal. Patient complained of having less sleep during the night due to an unfamiliar environment. An objective was set to restore her normal sleep pattern of 6-8 hours per night within 24 hours. Patient was reassured that quiet environment would be ensured and activities were organized for patient to prevent disturbing patient during sleep.
In the afternoon, routine vital signs were checked and medications served. Her lunch was rice and tomato stew after which she was served oranges.
Patient evening medications were served after she was done eating her supper. She was assisted to take her bath and brush her teeth. She was reassured her condition was improving.
Second day of admission (22th August, 2023)
On 22th August, 2023 thus third day of patient’s admission l arrived at the ward at 7:00am. According to the night staff, Mrs. L.K woke up around 6:30am she was assisted to empty her bowel and take her bath. Patient was able to sleep continuously for about 6-8hours last night as compared to the previous night. She was served with bread and porridge as breakfast. Vital signs were checked and recorded as;
Temperature		36.70C- 36.60C
Pulse 			70 beats per minute – 80 beats per minute
Respiration		20 cycles per minute- 22 cycles per minute
Blood pressure	165/80 mmHg
Her medications were served as prescribed and recorded. During ward rounds, patient had no complains but was ask to continue with her medications.
Patient was encouraged to take warm bath in the evening before going to bed. She was served with her evening medication and ate the food her daughter brought for her. They were reassured that her condition was improving. I took the opportunity to educate them on some of the causes of hypertension and its management such as the need to avoid taking high salt and cholesterol containing foods to add to what they already knew about the condition. Mrs. L.K was served her evening medication, assisted to take a warm bath and thereafter was allowed to do her bedtime rituals They were educated on the importance of complying with the treatment regimen. They both asked questions which were answered correctly and tactfully in simple terms.
Her bed linen was changed to make her bed comfortable and a quiet ward environment was ensured. Her due medication was served as well.
Third day of admission (23rd August, 2023)
My patient slept soundly throughout the night for about 6 hours according to the patient. She woke up and she was assisted to carry out her usual morning activities. According to the morning staff she was served with rice porridge and milk as breakfast. Vital signs were checked and recorded as;
Temperature		36.20C- 36.50C
Pulse 			85 beats per minute- 88 beats per minute
Respiration		20 cycles per minute- 22 cycles per minutes
Blood pressure	143/70mmHg
I was told she slept around 1pm in a relaxed ward environment and woke up at around 3:40pm. When she woke up, she was served her afternoon medications. Her daugther brought rice ball and groundnut soup for her as lunch which she ate only half. Thereafter, she was served with watermelon. After doctor rounds was over, he observed that she was recovering so quick.
Her knowledge on the condition was evaluated by asking questions concerning the causes, signs and symptoms, treatment, prevention and complication of hypertension. They both answered these questions correctly. I also added up and emphasized on the need to comply with the treatment regimen.
Patient evening medications were served. She was assisted to take a warm bath. Her bed linen was changed to make her comfortable. She was given Tablet diclofenac and tablet Lisinopril as prescribed. Miss L.K first home visit took place on this every day (22/08/23) while she is still on admission and I went together with her daughter.
Fourth Day of Admission (Day of Discharge), (24th August, 2023)
Patient woke up happily in the morning since she had a good night sleep and also because she could be discharged today. She took oats and bread as breakfast.
The vital signs were checked and it recorded as follows:
Temperature		36.00C
Pulse rate		70 beats per minute
Respiration 		18 cycles per minute
Blood pressure	120/80 millimeters of mercury
She was discharged during ward rounds to continue with her previous medications. Patient was able to mention some of the predisposing factors of hypertension and the relevance of following the treatment regimen even after being discharged. She was told to come for review on 31st August, 2023. She was taught how to take her drugs with the discharge plan. I assisted them in packing their belongings. Arrangements were made with her about my second home visit the following week before her review was due. They took a taxi and was bid farewell. Her particulars were entered into the Admission and Discharge book and the Daily Ward State. Her bed linen was removed and terminal decontamination done.

4.2The Preparation of Patient and Family for Discharge and Rehabilitation
Preparation of patient and family for discharge and rehabilitation began on the day of admission till the day of discharge. Patient and family members were reassured that client was to have only a temporary stay at the hospital so that she could get well. They were educated on the preventive measures of the condition as well as early reporting even before review. During the education, the following areas were stressed;
a) Diet and Modification of Lifestyle
Mrs. L.K and family were educated on the importance of a well-balanced diet in maintenance of good health. She was encouraged to continue taking low salt diet and fruits to eliminate anorexia. She was educated to take vegetables and vegetable oil since it is a source of unsaturated fat which helps to reduce the amount of cholesterol in the blood. She was also told to avoid taking non-prescribed drugs, herbal medicine, alcohol, fatty foods, high cholesterol diet, salt diet, smoking and stress.
b) Drugs and Review
The client and family were educated to continue with the treatment regimen as ordered to prevent relapse of her condition. Mrs. L.K was encouraged to come for review on the 31st August, 2023 and to report to the hospital any other day if the need arises. She was educated not to buy over the counter drugs but rather come to the hospital anytime symptoms reappear.
c) Exercise
Mrs. L.K and family were educated on the importance of regular tolerable exercise which would help improve her health status.
d) Rest and Sleep
Mrs. L.K was told to have sufficient rest and sleep. She was also educated on the importance of rest and sleep as it helps to repair the body’s worn-out tissues after a day’s work.


e) Personal and Environmental Hygiene
Mrs. L.K and her family were educated on the maintenance of good personal and environmental hygiene.
Client and relatives were happy upon discharge because she was going home and also because they had no bills to pay since they were subscribed with the National Health Insurance Scheme.

chapter: Chapter Four: Implementation Of Patient / Family Care Plan
heading: 4.3 The Home Visit / Follow –up
text:
4.3 The Home Visit / Follow –up
Home visit is a family-nurse contact which allows the health workers to assess the home and family situation in order to provide the necessary nursing care and health-related activities.
Follow up is done to ensure continuity of care for the patient before and after discharge from the hospital. Home visit is to help the nurse know how well the patient and family are doing to promote good health, prevent diseases and also give health education to the patient and family for continuity of care. For validation of data too.
First home visit Tuesday, 22nd August, 2023)
On this day at 11am, a visit was paid to Mrs. L.K house with her daughter, whom I had initially informed prior to the visit. The main aim was to find out about the patient’s home environment as well as health problems and possible solutions to them before patient is discharged. We boarded a car at Sunyani main station to their house at Sunyani-Area2. We walked for some few minutes on a duty road to the patient’s house which was right opposite the Stanbic Bank.  I was orientated to the house and its environs by her daughter. Mrs. L.K and his family live in hygienic compound. The house is built with cement and blocks and also well painted. The house is a story building contains three bed rooms, one big hall and general toilet and bath where all the tenants in the house use. It is roofed with iron sheets and plywood. They have good drainage and disposal system. The house has electricity and good source of water supply (pipe-borne water). Patient occupies a single room with her husband. The room has two windows at the opposite wall of the bed room. I told her daughter that I will give my maximum support to help her mother to recover fully after discharged.  I left there afterward around 12: 30 pm because of my afternoon shift and I had to check on my patient as well to know about her health status that day as well.
Second home visit (28th August, 2023)
The second home visit was made on the 28th August, 2023 to see how patient was doing and whether she was taking her drugs. The visit was also to remind them of the review date.
After a warm welcome, Mrs. L.K was asked how she was fairing. There were no complaints and patient looked well and healthy. She was then asked to bring the drugs so I could check whether she was taking them or not. I realized the drugs were being taken as ordered. Mrs. L.K was therefore congratulated and educated on the need to continue with the drugs to prevent any relapse of the disease condition and also eat a well-balanced diet in order to be healthy and also have enough rest and also encouraged her to engage in passive and active exercises daily. Her vital signs were also checked and recorded as follows: Temperature 36.1oC, Respiration 24cpm Pulse96 bpm, Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg.  Finally, I reminded them on the review date again, which is on 31th August, 2023.  Patient was also informed that I would terminate the care on my next home visit and will hand her over to a Public Health Nurse or a Community Health Nurse. They expressed their gratitude for the knowledge acquired and the care received from me. Permission was soughed and safely left     back home peacefully.
Review day (31stAugust 2023)
On the review day, patient and family were met at the outpatient’s department (OPD) at 7: 30am at the Sunyani Municipal hospital. They were warmly welcomed as we exchanged greetings with one another. I collected patient’s folder from the records room. Mrs. L.K   vital signs were checked and recorded as; Temperature 36.5, Pulse 84bpm, Respiration 22cpm, BP-130/90mmHg and was plotted accurately in the folder. Afterwards, it was sent to the nurse in the consulting room. She was examined by the doctor in-charge and was advised on the need to adhere to the treatment regimen. She was told to report for another review in a month’s time. We thanked the consulting team and headed towards the pharmacy to take her medications. After the medications were collected, it was quickly checked to know if all medications prescribed were received and also the expiry date and also assessed patient and family`s knowledge on the dosage, route of administration of the drug which was responded correctly. I thanked and escorted them to the car park where they picked a car back home.
Third home visit (2nd September, 2023)
The third home visit took place on at 10:00am. The aim of the visit was to assess patient on how she has been responding to treatment after the review and also to terminate the care given and hand her over to a community Health nurse for continuity of care. On arrival, patient was very fit and looked better. Patient also expressed a feeling of genuine sense of wellbeing as if she had never been sick. However, since the earlier stages of the nurse-patient/family relationship evolved effectively, the patient and family had a positive outlook and felt able to handle certain health problems independently.
Finally, the patient and family were made aware that my care has been terminated from that day but would continue to visit them once in a while. To this end, I also made it known to them that any health problem pertaining to Mrs. L.K condition should be reported to the Community Health Nurse for immediate intervention. They expressed their heartfelt gratitude for the immense contribution I had made towards their mother`s recovery. It was not easy parting ways with them but after some interaction with Mrs. L.K and her family, I asked if there were no further questions which needed clarification and I handed them over to the community health nurse then asked permission and left.

chapter: Chapter Five: Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Patient And Family
heading: 5.0 Introduction
text:
5.0 Introduction
The final phase of the nursing process is the evaluation phase. It takes place following the interventions to see if the goals have been met. During the evaluation phase, the nurse will determine how to measure the success of the goals and interventions. The responses are compared to expected outcomes to know the extent to which these outcomes have been achieved. The entire care plan is reassessed in this phase and any changes needed are made. The steps in evaluation of nursing care involve analyzing the patient’s responses, identifying factors contributing to success or failure and making amendments in the care plan if the expected outcomes are not met. It also consists of the termination of care rendered to the client/family.

chapter: Chapter Five: Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Patient And Family
heading: 5.1 Statement of evaluation
text:
5.1 Statement of evaluation
Mrs. L. K’s condition improved considerably with five days of admission. During the evaluation of nursing care rendered to him, all the goals were fully met. The evaluation was related to the problems presented by patient and the objective or outcome criteria.
 Patient presented with the following complains dizziness, headache, general body pains, palpitations and restlessness.
 Patient verbalized absence of headache
On 20th August, 2023, Patient complained of headache. An objective was set at 3pm to help relieve patient of her headache within 30 minutes. She was reassured that her comfort would be restored. Her bed was made free from creases to promote comfort. Mrs. L.K was provided with a radio set to serve as diversional therapy to take her mind of the pain. Tablet diclofenac 100mg was administered as prescribed. Goal was fully met at 3:30pm as patient verbalized a relief from headache.


Patient was able to perform daily activities
On 20th August, 2023, patient complained she was unable to perform daily activities. An objective was set at 2:55pm to help her perform daily activities within 24hours. She was reassured she will be relieved from her body weakness by some nursing measures that will be put in place. Patient`s items were brought close to her for easy reach and patient made good use of bed pan. Goals were fully met at 3pm the next day as patient verbalizing, she feels strong.
Patient was relieved from her dizziness
On the same day around 3:00pm, patient complained of dizziness. An objective was set and a nursing care plan drawn to help prevent her from sustaining any injury throughout her stay on the ward. Patient was reassured of speedy recovery. A complete bed rest was ensured. She was also assisted in doing all daily activities. She was nursed on a lower bed and bedside rails raised to prevent her from falls. Goal was fully met at 3:00pm on 21st August, 2023 as patient verbalized the absence of dizziness.
Patient was relieved from her palpitation
On the same day around 3:10pm, patient complained of palpitation. An objective was set and a nursing care plan was drawn to help prevent her from having decrease cardiac output. Patient was taught relaxation techniques to help reduce stress. Patient was reassured of speedy recovery. A complete bed rest was ensured.
Patient was relieved from having less sleep
On 21st August, 2023 at 8:20am, second day of admission, Mrs. L.K complained of having less sleep during the night due to an unfamiliar environment. An objective was set to restore her normal sleep pattern of 6-8 hours per night within 24 hours. Patient was reassured that quiet environment would be ensured and activities were organized for patient to prevent disturbing patient during sleep. Noise on the ward was reduced. Her bed linen was straightened and changed regularly to make her comfortable. Mrs. L.K was encouraged to sleep during the day. She was assisted to assume a comfortable position to enhance sleeping. Goal was fully met since client was observed to have slept soundly for 6-8hours during the night.
Patient was relieved from body weakness
On the 21st August, 2023, around 2:55pm, patient complain of body weakness. Patient could not groom herself so an objective was set and a nursing care plan was drawn so she was assisted to brush her teeth and visit the toilet and took her bath. Her medications were served accordingly and recorded. During ward rounds, the lab results were shown to the doctor and she confirmed that everything was normal.
Patient expressed understanding of Hypertension
During an interaction with patient at 8:40am on the 22nd August, 2023, it was revealed that patient did not have adequate knowledge about her condition. Hence a care plan with knowledge deficit related to inadequate information on disease condition as diagnosis with an objective set to ensure that patient is able to express understanding of hypertension within 2hours. At 10:30am on the same day, the goal set at 9:30am was evaluated and the goal was fully met as nurse observed patient state the causes and signs and symptoms of Hypertension.

5.2 Amendment of Nursing Care for Partially Met or Unmet Outcome Criteria
No amendments were made to the nursing care plan drawn for Mrs. L.K and family throughout her period of stay on the ward since both patient and family gave their maximum co-operation in the achievement of the set goals. And also, with the help of the holistic nursing care provided by our competent nursing team.

chapter: Chapter Five: Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Patient And Family
heading: 5.3 Termination of care
text:
5.3 Termination of care
Termination of care is ending interactions with patient and family. Termination is a difficult step to be taken after a good rapport has been established, for that reason the reality of termination was started on the first day of admission, 20th August, 2023. Patient and family were made to understand, that my relationship with them was a therapeutic one and will come to an end after his recovery, but on discharge the care shall be continued by the health care team in the hospital since it is the nearest hospital. Patient and her relatives were educated on her care and reassured that she would recover and eventually be discharged on admission, she was given good nursing care. Follow up visits were made and it was found out that patient condition had improved significantly. She and her family were educated on how to maintain good personal and environmental hygiene and the need to take a well-balanced diet. She was advised to stick to prescribed drug regimen and also advised to report to the nearest hospital which is closer to them in case of any illness and to ensure continuity of care. The termination was successfully done on 2nd h September, 2023 during my third home visit. Patient was handed over to a nurse in the same hospital.

heading: 5.4 Summary of care rendered to patient and family
text:
5.4 Summary of care rendered to patient and family
Mrs. L.K, a 48-year-old woman was admitted at the Emergency ward on 20th August, 2023 at the Sunyani municipal hospital. Patient was diagnosed as having hypertension. The following investigation were requested for him; Full blood count, Blood film for malaria parasites, Chest x-ray, fasting Blood glucose and urine routine examination. She was managed on intravenous hydralazine, Tablet Nifedipine, Tablet Lisinopril, Tablet Bendroflomethiazide, intravenous cefuroxime and Tablet diclofenac. Throughout patient’s admission, nursing problems identified on patient were restlessness, headache, dizziness, joint pains, palpitations and general body pains. With the appropriate nursing care rendered, these problems were identified and goals set to alleviate the problems were fully met before the day of discharge. Medications prescribed by the doctor were served and patient responded to treatment. Mrs. L.K. was discharged on 25th August, 2023.Her condition had improved remarkably. Follow up visits were made after discharge to ensure continuity of care. Care was finally terminated on 2nd September, 2023 and patient was handed over to a nurse in charge at the OPD in the same hospital

PREFACE
The study of patient and family care stands as a crucial aspect of nursing care provided to patients and their families enduring a health condition during hospitalization and post-discharge. This in-depth exploration equips student nurses with essential skills—assessing and diagnosing the health issues of the patient, devising a comprehensive nursing care plan, executing the plan to address the health needs of both the patient and their family, and critically evaluating the effectiveness of the nursing care rendered.
This care study is undertaken and documented as a mandatory requirement, a significant step toward obtaining a registered nurse license, as stipulated by the Nursing and Midwifery Council for Ghana.
Beyond fulfilling regulatory requirements, the patient and family care study serves as a valuable source of both theoretical and practical knowledge. Student nurses delve into extensive research to gain a nuanced understanding of their patient's condition, bridging the gap between classroom learning and real-world application. Importantly, it fosters a meaningful interpersonal connection between the student nurse and the patient's family, enhancing the quality of care provided.
Furthermore, this study serves a dual purpose by becoming a valuable resource for literature review. It offers students an opportunity to explore and comprehend the intricacies of specific disease conditions, contributing to their academic growth and knowledge expansion.
In essence, the patient and family care study transcends a mere academic exercise; it represents a pivotal journey in a student nurse's education, nurturing skills, empathy, and understanding essential for the compassionate delivery of healthcare.

INTRODUCTION
This report details the comprehensive nursing care provided to Miss P.A, a 10-year-old girl admitted to Bono Regional Hospital on August 23, 2023. She was brought in by her parents and relatives, presenting symptoms including dyspnea, chest and hip pain, fever, dizziness, coughing, and pallor. The initial diagnosis at the pediatric emergency was acute chest syndrome secondary to sickle cell disease, leading to her subsequent admission to the pediatric ward.
Upon discussing the intention of conducting a care study with Miss P.A and her family, they generously granted their consent, allowing me to delve into understanding her disease condition. A genuine connection was formed through empathetic conversations, paving the way for this insightful project.
The patient underwent a thorough assessment, leading to the development and implementation of a comprehensive nursing care plan targeting her health issues. Thanks to prompt medical attention and effective nursing interventions, Miss P.A experienced a swift and complete recovery, leading to her discharge on August 28, 2023, after a five-day hospital stay.
The care extended beyond the hospital, with three home visits conducted to assess the environment, monitor her well-being, and provide additional education. This report is organized into five chapters:
Chapter One: Covers the assessment of the patient and family.
Chapter Two: Encompasses the analysis of collected data.
Chapter Three: Outlines the plan for patient and family care.
Chapter Four: Explores the implementation of the care plan.
Chapter Five: Evaluates the care rendered to the patient and her family.

chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of Patient And Family
heading: Introduction
text:
Introduction
A well-structured or systematic approach of eliciting and assembling of patient and/or family actual, potential and possible health problems is termed as nursing assessment (Jarvis, 2023). Assessment emanates as the most immediate step of the nursing process and it utilizes conscious and comprehensive observation, collection and documentation of deviated and inappropriate health patterns of patient or family. Scrutinization of patient for health problems employs inspection, auscultation, palpitation, and percussion to detect abnormalities, instabilities and inconsistencies in an individual’s health. Sources of health problems or data can be majorly categorized into three. Primary; which are data taken from the patient directly, secondary; data sourced from the relatives of patient and documentations and reports pertinent to the patient and tertiary; data derived from journals, articles and textbooks. During assessment or interview of patient for health problems, complaints or data received from patient can be either subjective or objective depending how overt or covert it is. Assessment is generally imperative, since the problems affecting the patient can be closely identified and dealt with accordingly to improve patient condition correspondingly.
The Patient’s Particulars
Patient particulars encompass all the relevant data about a patient that are necessary for providing appropriate medical care. Miss P.A is a 10 year old girl and the fifth child of Mr. E.A and Mrs. L.A born in Sunyani at Sunyani Municipal Hospital on 11th October, 2012. Miss P.A comes from Damango in the Savanna region and also together with her family is a Christian and attends church at Deeper Life Ministry Church at Abesim, also their place of residence with their house number H6/16. She schools at Abesim SDA primary school and is in class 5. She has 6 siblings and speaks and understands English, Gonja and Twi. She is 1.47m tall and weighs 24kg and also fair in complexion. She appraises her elder sister J.A to be her next of kin.
The Family’s Medical History
This section deals with the collection of data from patient about some genetic or familial predispositions and risks factors or routines that could be associated with or contribute to the present health condition (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 2023). Her mother stated that, she has a normal heamoglobin genotype of HgAc but is Miss P.A’s father who has sickle cell trait or is a carrier, one of her aunties also developed the condition in the preadolescent stage but could manage through adulthood and is now better with minimal or sometimes absence of complications of the sickling condition. Except for the sickle cell disease, they have not identified any genetic or lineal-predisposed medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, and tumors among others as far as the mother can recall. Due to changes in whether conditions and other factors she is oftentimes hospitalized. She uses over the counter medications for pain relief, blood tonics for nourishment among others. She has not identified any allergies yet and could tolerate almost every meal or drug.

chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of Patient And Family
heading: 1.3 The Patient's Socioeconomic History
text:
1.3 The Patient’s Socioeconomic History
Miss P.A is the reserved type and does not often mingle or be with friends or colleagues except for her siblings, parent and other relatives who she relates very well with at home. Her mother revealed that she only indulges in passive recreational activities such as playing Ludo or playing video games on the phone. Miss P.A is respectful, calm and always ready to learn and is heavily supported by her immediate family members, friends and some other relatives. Her mother affirmed that, she totally depends on her parents for all her financial needs and has the National Health Insurance Scheme Id card for all her medical care bills.
The Patient’s Developmental History
Growth can be best defined as the irreversible improvement of the size of an organism over a period of time (Biology Online, 2023). Development on the hand can be defined as an expansion of human capabilities and the enhancement in the skills and overall performance of same or previous activities (Mahendra, 2023). Whilst maturation is the genetically programmed process involved in developing social, emotional or psychological mechanisms to become more adaptable to real life issues (Lalit, 2023). Miss P.A has successfully passed through her developmental process from birth till the current stage of her development. Her mother affirmed that she gave birth to her through spontaneous vaginal delivery without any complications such as prolonged labour, congenital abnormalities, etc. She begun to sit and crawl when she was around 4 to 6 months old, stood up and learned to walk by the 8th to 12th months. Respectfully, she was exclusively breastfed for the first 6 months, and subsequently introduced to complimentary feeds from there. In comparison of her developmental status with Erik Erickson’s psychosocial development theory, she belongs to the industry versus inferiority stage, which spells out that individual who are at this developmental level tend to indulge in domestic, communal, and school chores of which they expect to be acknowledged and praised of it when successfully pursued. On the contrary, if they become unsuccessful in performing these chores they fell embarrassed and inferior among their peers who are capable. Miss P.A has succeeded in this stage and feels industrious since she can perform most of the task expected of her like bathing self, washing utensils, sweeping the compound among others. Significant Secondary sexual characteristics like breast, pubic hairs, and hip enlargement have not been apparently seen yet, although she reported about tiny hair growth under the armpit and her genital. She was vaccinated against the vaccine preventable diseases including polio, diphtheria, and measles among others. She dreams of becoming a nurse when she grows up.

chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of Patient And Family
heading: 1.4 The Patient's Lifestyle/Hobbies
text:
1.4 The Patient’s Lifestyle/Hobbies
Miss P.A normally wakes up at 6:00am, her mother attested to her participation in the morning devotions they normally have each morning around 6:15 – 6:30am after she’s performed some early personal hygiene activities like brushing of teeth mostly with Colgate toothpaste and evacuating the bowels. Normally she takes her shower twice a day around 6:45am and 6:00pm with Geisha bathing soap. She has her personal bathing towel, toothbrush, sponge and other personal hygiene equipment and does not share them with anyone. Her mother appreciates her ability to perform some instrumental activities of daily living such as washing, assisting in house chores like cooking and making of phone calls with her other relatives when she does not have the crises. Without the sickle cell complications she is able to attend school throughout the weekdays, performs her assignments right after school. She is also able to do some laundry, washing of dishes, attending church services and activities during the weekends. She is able to eliminate her bowels and bladder two to three times daily. Mother of miss P.A highlighted that, food is normally prepared three times throughout the day of which she enjoys eating plain rice with tomato sauce. She usually goes to bed before 10:00pm and is able to have good sleep without difficulties. She has not identified any allergic reaction to food nor drugs. She likes reading a lot of story books and her favorite is “The Water Princess” and also sometimes watches television at her leisure. She relates utterly well with her siblings, parents and friends.

Miss P.A even though was known to have Sickle Cell Disease, she looked absolutely healthy and had no signs of complications of the condition until on 23rd August, 2023 when she started having extreme chest and back pain, difficulty in breathing, coughing, fever, malaise and dizziness in the morning and was sent to the pediatric emergency ward of Bono Regional hospital around 3:00pm with her mother, father and other accompanying relatives. 1.7 Admission Of The Patient
At 3:00pm on 23rd August, 2023, miss P.A attended the paediatric unit of Bono Regional hospital through the emergency department with severe chest and back pain and difficulty in breathing. She was brought in by wheelchair and accompanied by her mother and other close relatives. Miss P.A and her relatives were passionately attended to and welcomed. Confirmation of admission of patient was commenced by keying her Id number thus AAl7620 into the LHIMS to have access to her folder and crosscheck her details. Miss P.A and relatives were given seats to rest and wait. Soon after, an admission bed was prepared and she was put onto it and made comfortable by positioning her in a Fowler’s position in order to improve her lung expansion, capacity and improve her oxygenation. Her vital signs were checked and recorded as;
Temperature – 37.8°C
Pulse – 128bpm
Respiratory rate – 39cpm
Oxygen saturation rate – 96%
Weight – 24kg
Quick head to toe assessment was done on her and the health problems identified included; Dyspnea, chest and hip pain, fever, dizziness, coughing and pallor. At 3:10pm she was administered with oxygen 2L/min via nasal prongs and then infused with IV normal saline 500mls at 62mls/hour. Investigations requested to be carried out were full blood count, chest x-ray and pleural tap investigation. From the emergency report, she was a known sickle cell patient and diagnosed with acute chest syndrome. The following were the further treatment prescribed and planned for miss P.A during the admission period till her discharge;
IV normal saline 500mls stat
IV ceftriaxone 2g od  x 6 days
IV Paracetamol 360ml tid x 6 days
Tab ibuprofen 200mg tid x 5 days
Tab Azithromycin 250mg od x 4 days
Syrup Zincovit 10mls 0d x 4 days
IV Fluocloxacillin 600mg qid x 5 days
Tab Folic acid 5mg od  x 30 days
Tab Hyroxyurea 500mg od  x 30days
Admission procedure and other relevant information were taken and recorded in the required recording documents those are the nurses’ notes, admission and discharge book and the daily ward state. I quickly approached and greeted them and introduced myself and the name of the ward. I further orientated her mother by showing her around some of the facilities and surroundings in the ward such as the nurses’ station, washroom and others. I then introduced her and her mother to the other patient that her daughter was going to share the same cubicle with. She was then educated on the daily ward routines such as visiting hours (5:30am – 6:00am and 4:30-6:00pm), meals time (breakfast; 8:00am, lunch; 12:00pm and supper; 5:00pm) and ward rounds which mainly occurs on Tuesdays. They also learned about the vital signs monitoring hours and time medications were administered thus; 6:00am, 10:00am, 2:00pm, 6:00pm and 10:00pm every day. Finally, I conferred with her and her family the intension of embarking a project known as care study with her, which resulted in long conversation but eventually gave their consent for me to proceed.
