chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of The Patient/Family
heading: Introduction
text:
Introduction
This chapter marks the initial phase of the nursing process. It considers the physical, social, emotional, developmental, intellectual and spiritual aspect of the individual. It entails the collection of data from the patient, relative, friends, neighbors and medical records. The data collected severs as a benchmark for the identification of patient/family health problem. This phase begins the interaction with the patient and family during the time of admission.
Patient’s Particulars
According to APA Dictionary of psychology, Biographical data is the information about patient’s history and behavioral patient, gathered by therapist or medical professional primarily from the patient but sometimes from the others who knows much about the patients or his relatives. Patient particulars are the personal information that the health provider collects from patient, such as their name, date of birth, address and medical history. The sources of this information can include the patients themselves, family members, others healthcare provider’s medical records. It is important to keep this information confidential and secure in order to protect the patient’s privacy. Mrs. Y.A is the name of my patient. She was born on the 25th October, 1966 and she is55 years of age. Mrs. Y.A comes from Sunyani a city located in the Bono Region but stays at Fiapre. She was born to Mr. O.I and Mrs. F.B. She’s the first born of her parents. She’s dark in complexion and weighs 54kg. She’s 1.4 meters tall .She’s a Christian and worships with her family at the Church of Pentecost at Fiapre.
Family Medical And Socio- Economic History
According to America Academy of family physicians, (2018) family medical and socio-economic history is defined as the collection of information about the patient’s family, medical, and socio history, including information about the patient’s occupation, income education, and living situation as well as relevant medical history of family members. This information can help health care providers to better understand a patient’s risk and need and to develop a more personalized treatment plan. This source of this information comes from the patient themselves as well as family members, medical records, and other healthcare providers. Mrs. Y.A belongs to an extended family which consists of her mother, Siblings, Uncle, Auntie, Her children of three and her husband. All her siblings are alive and healthy. Both grandparents are late, they had a peaceful death. Her father died out of car accident. She disclosed that there is no certain disease in her family. She however added that they often suffer from malaria and is normally treated on outpatient basis at a nearby hospital. Mrs. Y.A is the only one suffering from pneumonia. She said she don’t remember the last time she came to the infirmary. The sources of medical treatment are herbal and orthodox. No known allergies. Mrs. Y.A uses over - the - counter drugs like Paracetamol and Martins liver salts. She works as a trader at the Wednesday market. She attends funerals, weddings and church convention. She relate with her family well. Mrs. Y.A and her family get their support from their farming and marketing activities for their living. She is the head of women’s followership at the church of Pentecost. She at times visit Sunyani Municipal hospital and is supported by her husband financially. Due to her occupation, patient is likely to get bites. Mrs. Y.A said she does not know the income per year but for some months she can get GH₵ 500. The family support themselves with the farm and the marketing. Patient taboo is that they don’t go to farm on Wednesdays.
Patient’s Developmental And History
According to Mrs. Y.A, her mother told her she was born spontaneous vagina delivery and received all childhood vaccines for preventable diseases. She started crawling when she was six months old and her teeth started erupting at the same age. She could stand when she was eleven months and started walking when she was one year old. At the age of 12 years, Mrs. Y.A had her first menarche. Mrs. Y.A said she wanted to be a Teacher. Mrs. Y.A is married to Mr. A.C and she’s not a widow. She’s at her menopause stage and she does not remember when it started. She works as a trader; she sells tomatoes at the market.
Patient Lifestyle/ Hobbies
According to Mrs. Y.A, She wakes up by 5:00AM and prays before going out. She cares for her teeth with Pepsodent tooth paste and toothbrush; she takes her bath with clean water, sponge, soap and a towel. She takes her breakfast and goes to the market to sell tomatoes. At her leisure time she chats with her friends at the market. She also likes listening to high life songs. She goes to market during week days (Mondays – Fridays). She goes to work on Saturdays but not most of the times and goes to church on Sundays. She has no difficulties in eating, walking, and grooming. She has no personal habit, such as the use of tobacco, alcohol, coffee, illicit drugs and recreational drugs. Mrs. Y.A said she empty her bladder thrice daily and bowel thrice a week early in the morning before taking her bath. She takes in typical diet thrice daily, And her daughter does the cooking. She only buys food when she didn’t bring food to the market. She takes in Hausa Koko with koose for breakfast, Ampesi with garden egg stew for lunch and fufu with light soup for supper. Mrs. Y.A said she wake up mostly around 5:00 AM each day and goes to bed around 8:10PM at night, she sleeps well most of the night. She has no known allergies. She likes playing oware. She likes listening to music and she dislikes a noisy environment. She’s sociable. Mrs. Y.A takes the roles of a wife and a grandmother. She worships with the church of Pentecost and also the head of women’s fellowship. She likes listening to music like high life and likes dancing with the song. She does exercise by walking around her house. She normally goes for social activities such as weddings, funeral and church.
Past Medical/Surgical/Obstetrics History
According to Mrs. Y.A she never suffered from any serious illness during her childhood days. However, she developed minor ailments such as headache, fever, chills, abdominal pains and she was managed with orthodox drugs. She had no accident and injury.

chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of The Patient/Family
heading: 1.9 Literature Review
text:
1.9 Literature Review
Anatomy And Physiology Review Of The Respiratory System
The cells of the body need energy for all their metabolic activities. Most of this energy is derived from chemical reactions, which can only take place in presence of oxygen. The main waste product of this reaction is carbon dioxide. The respiratory system provides the route by which the supply of oxygen present in the atmospheric air enters the body, and it provides the route of excretion for carbon dioxide. The organs of the respiratory system are; nose, pharynx, trachea, two bronchi, bronchioles and smaller air passage, two lungs and their coverings (the pleural muscles of respiration.
Bronchi And Bronchioles
The two primary bronchi are formed when the trachea divides at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebrae that is the right and left bronchus. The bronchial walls are composed of the same tissue as the trachea is lined with ciliated columnar epithelium. The bronchi progressively subdivide into bronchioles, terminal bronchioles, respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts and finally alveoli. The wider passages are called conducting airways because their function is to bring air into the lungs, and their thick walls too permit gas exchange.( Smelter and Bare 2010)
Pneumonia
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung tissue commonly caused by bacterial, viruses or fungi in which the lungs undergone consolidation. (Toohey, 1994)
Incidence and prevalence
About 3 million cases of pneumonia are reported each year. Of these, about one-third occurs in people over age 65. Approximately, 4 out of every 100 children in the United States develop pneumonia each year and about 60,000 people die as a result of the condition.
It is also common among people who work in industries such as mining, construction and people exposed to noxious gas and heavy smokers.
Aetiology
Pneumococci are the main causative organisms of pneumonia however it may be caused by;
Infection from viruses, bacteria, parasites, fungi, etc.
Aspiration of stomach content into the lungs.
Inhalation of dust.
Inhalation of irritative gases such as fumes.
Radiation therapy for breast or lung cancer.
Predisposing factors
Prolong immobility and shallow breathing pattern.
Respiratory therapy with improperly cleaned equipment.
Depressed cough reflex due to medication or weakened respiratory muscles.
Advanced age, due to possible depressed cough and gag reflex.
Weakened immune system or body’s natural defence mechanism. Example, cancer or HIV AIDS.
Impaired gas reflex, example seizures.
Placement of nasogastric or endotracheal tube.
Conditions that produce mucous or bronchial obstruction and interfere breathing pattern
Frequent exposure to cigarette smoke can affect the lungs in ways that make a person more likely to develop pneumonia.
Inhalation of heavy dust and irritative gases such as fumes.
Conditions such as lung disease, heart disease, stroke and seizure.
Types
The types of pneumonia are classified under the following:
By aetiology:
Infection from viruses, bacteria, parasites, fungi, etc.
Aspiration of stomach content into the lungs.
Inhalation of irritative gases
By anatomical position
Lobar or segmental pneumonia: it occurs when a substantial portion of one or more lobes of the lung are involved. Example, right upper lobar pneumonia which shows the pneumonia is affecting the upper lobe of the right lung.
Bronchopneumonia: it is when small areas of the lung alveoli and lobules around small terminal bronchi are affected.
Lobular pneumonia: this is when a lobe is involved.
Pathophysiology
Pneumonia usually starts when a person inhales infected air particles into the lungs. In other cases, it develops during or after a viral upper respiratory infection, such as a cold or the flu or from aspiration of gastric content and normal flora of the upper respiratory tract into the lung. Once the bacteria, virus or fungus enter the lungs, they usually settle in the air sacs of the lung where they rapidly grow in number. An inflammatory reaction initiated by the causative organism occurs in the alveoli, producing exudates as the body attempts to fight off the infection. which interferes with the diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide, white blood cells mostly neutrophils, also migrate into the alveoli and fill the normally air containing spaces. Areas of the lung are not adequately ventilated because of secretions and mucosal oedema that causes partial occlusion of the bronchi or alveoli, with a resultant decrease in alveolar oxygen tension. Bronchospasm may also occur in a patient, hypoventilation, a ventilation perfusion mismatch occurs in the affected area of the lung. Various blood entering the pulmonary circulation passes through the under ventilated area and exits to the left side of the heart poorly oxygenated. The mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated or poorly oxygenated blood eventually results in arterial hypoxemia.
Clinical manifestation
Cough
Pleuritic chest pain (aggravated by breathing and coughing)
Rapid pulse
Fever which usually ranges from (38.0oC - 40.5oC)
Poor appetite
Shortness of breath
Headache
Bradycardia
Rapid shallow respiration
Unproductive cough during unset and latter productive
Difficulty in breathing
Cyanosis
Weakness
Nausea
Diagnostic investigations
Chest X-ray to assess the anatomical structure of the lung by showing a dense shadow at the affected part. Chest x-rays can reveal areas (seen as white) which represent consolidation.
Chest CT (computed tomography) can reveal pneumonia that is not seen on chest x-ray.
Sputum specimen for gram stain and culture and sensitivity test which may show acute inflammatory cells and the causative organism and its sensitive antibiotic.
Routine sputum culture
A complete blood count may show a high white blood cell count, indicating the presence of an infection or inflammation.
Sputum for  Acid Fast Bacilli to rule out TB
Sputum specimen for gram stain and culture and sensitivity test may show acute inflammatory cell and the causative organism.
Blood analysis may show high erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR).
Lung needle biopsy
Physical examination
History and signs and symptoms of the patient will help.
Bronchoscopy or transtracheal aspiration allows the collection of materials for culture or biopsy.
Pulse oximetry may show a reduced arterial o
Oxygen saturation level.
Medical treatment
Treatment depends much on preventing any complication and to cure the infection. However, the patient is given the following drugs;
Antimicrobial therapy such as cefuroxime, high dose of amoxicillin is given based on the causative agent, Erythromycin may be given if the organism is not known in other to prevent or fight infection.
Analgesics such as Diclofenac and salicylates to relieve pain.
Antipyretic drugs such as acetaminophen are given to relieve fever or pyrexia.
Haematinics to prevent anaemia such as folic acid.
Expectorants, example Simple linctus cough mixture can be prescribed to reduce cough and increase expectoration of sputum.
Intravenous fluid therapy may be prescribed for fever and dehydration.
Provision of nutrients and to maintain electrolyte balance. Examples of these fluids are ringers lactate, normal saline and dextrose saline.
Other non-pharmacological therapy may include;
Respiratory support measures such as humidified oxygen, endotracheal intubation, high inspiration oxygen concentration, mechanical ventilation and positive end expiration pressure (PEEP) may help in treating hypoxia that may result from either shortness of breath or Dyspnoea.
Pneumodectomy ; A surgical removal of an entire lung may be needed if the infection is prone to or leads to complications such as lung abscess
Nursing management
Psychological Care:
Patients with pneumonia usually have respiratory distress with anxiety. Therefore, there should be the need to provide psychological support by assuming the client of the necessary nursing care to allay anxiety. This should be done by reassuring the client on her condition in other to win her cooperation, confidence and establish rapport. The measures may include diversional therapy, such as watching television and engaging in conversation with the client.
Observation
Monitor vital signs, temperature (38.7℃), pulse, respiration and blood pressure four hourly when necessary paying attentions on respiration rate and character of breathe sound, and temperature.
Monitor fluid intake and output to prevent circulation overload. Monitor nutritional intake to encourage the intake of carbohydrate and protein if not properly taken to help fight infection.
Sputum should be observed for amount, odor, consistency, and presence of blood or any other material.
Evaluate the effect of the administered medication and observe for their adverse effect or reactions if any.
Maintenance of normal body temperature
Since fever is a persistent problem, the temperature is monitored regularly. If temperature exceeds normal, the client is tepid sponged, serve cold drinks and make sure there is adequate ventilation which may all help reduce temperature to normal.
Prescribed antipyretics are also served while limiting cloths on client.
Position
Client should be kept in an upright or semi-fowlers position to reduce stress and conserve energy, for proper lung expansion to enhance patency of airway and comfort.
The patient may also be encouraged to lie on the affected lung side to splint the chest and reduce pleural rubbing that often causes discomfort.
Client should also change positions frequently to enhance secretion clearance and ventilation/perfusion in the lungs.
Rest and sleep.
The nurse encourages the debilitated patient to rest and avoid overexertion and possible exacerbation of symptoms.
Measures to encourage rest and sleep such as calm environment, warm bath and drinks, nursing patient in a dim light, provision of properly made bed without creases and crumps, changing of soiled bed linen, ensuring good ventilation by opening windows to allow fresh air.
Maintenance of patent airway
Retained secretion interferes with gas exchange which may slow recovery.
In this case hydration should be encouraged to loosen pulmonary secretion.
The nurse should also perform chest physiotherapy to loosen and mobilize secretion and make them responsive to spontaneous or directed cough to clear the airway.
The patient is also encouraged to exercise deep breathing and coughing at least every 2 hours and also at least 3 litters of oral fluids per day to help expectorate secretions after raising the head end of the bed to at least 45 degrees.
Personal Hygiene
Encourage bathing at least twice daily.
Mouth care is given regularly to combat dryness or cracking of the lips that might result from fever or dehydration, the lip can be kept supply of Vaseline,
Change dirty clothing and soiled linen.
Nutrition
1. Light nourishing diet should be encouraged.
2. Clients diet should contain high calories to provide patient with energy since there is labored breathing. Protein and vitamin food should also be provided.
3. Increased nutrition help repair won out tissues and boost the clients immunity against infections.
4. Gas forming foods should be avoided to prevent the occurrence of abdominal distension.
Fluid intake
Dehydration is a potential problem due to fever and dyspnea. Therefore, fluid intake is encouraged at least 2 litters per day to help thin secretions.
Carefully records on oral and parental intake and output charts should be kept.
Signs of over-hydration should be observed when client is on intravenous fluids.
Chemotherapy
Drugs prescribed by the physician are served and charted in the drug administration chart accordingly.
Clients are to be monitored for any adverse reactions of the drugs.
Education
Advise client to dispose all secretions properly, sneeze or cough into a disposable tissues to prevent spread of infection.
Educate the client on the need to cover the chest and the rest of the body especially when the weather is cold.
Advise the client to complete the entire course of medication.
Also educate client on the importance of periodic check-up and review and report for medical advice anytime signs and symptoms reappear.
Complications
Atelectasis
Pleural effusion
Pericarditis
Lung abscess
Endocarditis
Meningitis
Cardiac failure
Lung fibrosis
Pulmonary oedema
Respiratory circulatory failure
Septicaemia
Septic shock

heading: Introduction
text:
Introduction
ASSESSMENT is the first step in the nursing process. It involves gathering of information about the health status of the patient/client, analysis and synthesis of the data and making of clinical nursing judgment. Assessment of patient and family deals with collection of data on patient’s medical records, family account, examination, interviews, and other health team members. This chapter comprises of patient particularsꓼ the patient family medical history, socio-economic history, patient’s development history, patient’s lifestyle∕ hobbies, past medical history, patients present medical history, and admission of patient.
Patient’s Particulars
Particulars are facts or details such as; name, sex, religion, ethnicity, and date of birth, among others, about the patient which is written down and kept as a record (Wang & Peura, 2015). Madam B.O is a 22-year-old woman, born on the 10th April,2001 to Mr P.O and Madam E.P of Kumasi Asawase in the Asokore manpong Municipality. She is an Akan by tribe and a Ghanaian by nationality. Madam B.O is from Nsona clan and the third child among 12 of her parents. Madam B.O stays at Mayfair in Sunyani. She is fair in complexion and speaks Twi and English. She is a business woman. She attended school up to JHS 3 thus; she attended at Asawasi Pentecost School. She married to Mr K.Y and they have two children (2 female) who are both alive. Madam B.O weighs 69 kilogram (kg) and has a height of 165 centimetres (cm). Her next of kin is her husband Mr K.Y. Madam B.O is a Christian and attends the church of house of power

heading: 1.4 Patient's Developmental History
text:
1.4 Patient’s Developmental History
Developmental history is an account of how and when a person met developmental milestones such as; walking and talking (Shiel, 2016). Growth is defined as the progressive development of a living thing, especially the process by which the body reaches its point of complete physical development. Development on the other hand is defined as the process of growth and differentiation. It includes cognitive development, psychosexual development and psychosocial development. Development is a continuous and gradual process. Maturation is simply defined as ripening or developing (Weller, 2009). According to Madam B.O, her mother told her she was delivered via a spontaneous vaginal delivery at the hospital. She had no difficulties or problems during pregnancy, labour, delivery, and throughout breastfeeding her. Congenital anomalies such as cleft lip and palate and hydrocephalous were absent. She was immunized against the childhood preventable diseases on the right hand. So she did not suffer any of such diseases that might have retarded her growth. She went through normal developmental milestones such as sitting, crawling, standing, walking and running. Madam B.O claimed she could sit by four months, had her teeth erupted at six months, crawled by nine months, stood up by a year, and walked and talked by a year and a half although she could make some sounds such as mama and dada as early as six months. A couple of months later, she could act on instructions like ‘go and ‘come’. Madam B.O said she was not exclusively breastfed. Her mother started serving her complementary foods at five months as she did with all of her siblings. She could take care of her daily personal hygiene activities such as bathing, brushing her teeth and dressing up under little or no supervision at the age of five years. She developed secondary sexual characteristics such as menstruation (menarche), enlargement of breast and appearance of pubic hair at the age of sixteen. Madam B.O started schooling at the age of five beginning with preschool and drop out of school at JHS3 at the age of sixteen years. She got pregnant for Mr. K.Y and had first child at the age of nineteen. According to Erik Erikson’s psychosocial theory, humans experience eight stages of development over their lifespan, from infancy through late adulthood, at each stage there’s a crisis or task that needs to be resolved. Successful completion of each developmental task results in a sense of competence and a healthy personality. Failure to master these tasks leads to feelings of inadequacy (Sacco, 2013). My patient Madam B.O was 22 years old and therefore she was within the early adulthood stage of Erik Erikson’s theory. This stage is known as intimacy versus isolation which ranges between the ages of (19-29 years) (Sacco, 2013).

text:
1.8 Admission Of The Patient
Madam B.O was admitted into the female medical ward of the Sunyani Municipal Hospital through the OPD on the 17th August, 2023 by P.A Janice at 2:35pm .With two relatives and an accompanying nurse in a wheelchair with the diagnosis of Malaria. They were warmly welcomed at the entrance of the ward and they were escorted to the nurse’s station. They were offered seats, and I introduced the nurses present as well, the hospital was using the paperless system (LHIMS) therefore, patient’s identity, diagnoses, medications and investigations among other particulars were crosschecked on the system for confirmation purposes.  The patient was weak but in a conscious state upon arrival. She was admitted with a history of abdominal pain, headache, vomiting and fever. She and her relatives were reassured of competent nursing care and were encouraged to verbalize fears and ask questions or anything they need to know or have concerns about. She was then sent to her bedside and made comfortable in an already prepared admission bed devoid of creases and cramps. She was introduced to the patients near her. Her valuable items were put in her bedside locker as per the hospital policy. They were also orientated to the ward and were also informed of the visiting hours, morning at 5:30am to 6:30am, afternoon 12:00pm to 1:00pm and at 4:30pm to 5:30pm and the time for ward rounds. Her admission details were documented in the admission and discharge book and daily ward state. I introduced myself as a student of the Nursing and Midwifery Training College, Seikwa (SNMTC) who wants to use her to write my care study as part of the requirement for the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) which she and her family accepted and promised me of their cooperation. From observation, she was anxious as a result of the unknown outcome of her disease condition and her baby. Her mother assured her that she will take good care of the baby and she was again reassured by the staff that she was in competent hands and everything will be made possible to facilitate speedy recovery so that she would be discharged home successfully as early as possible. Vital signs were checked and recorded as follows;
Temperature………….36.8 degrees Celsius
Pulse………………… 99 beats per minute (bpm)

Blood Pressure……………105/62 millimetres of mercury (mmHg)

The following laboratory investigations were also requested.

Urine for Routine Examination.
The physician was assisted to take blood sample for the laboratory investigations. The patient was put on the following medications;

The patient was served with tablet paracetamol 1g and was informed that whilst on admission, she would need items such as a toothbrush and paste, sponge and towel, bathroom sandals, pail, comb, pomade, powder, dresses, plate, spoon and cup to help cater for her immediate needs. Her immediate needs were gathered through observation and interviews using the nursing process and a care plan were drawn for her. chapter: Chapter One: Assessment Of Patient And Her Family
heading: 1.9 Patient's Concept Of Her Illness
text:
1.9 Patient’s Concept Of Her Illness
Madam B.O did not attribute her illness to superstitious beliefs or any spiritual cause but she believes that her illness was caused by a bite of mosquito. She also believed that by the grace of God and with the help of medical treatment and nursing intervention, she will regain her strength
1.10LITERATURE REVIEW
The literature review gives a clear picture of the disease condition. It also helps the student nurse compare with the disease process presented by the patient
Definition
According to Weller (2009), malaria is an infection of the red blood cell caused by plasmodium, a single cell organism. The disease is however characterized by periodic chills, fever, sweating and splenomegaly. According to Porter (2012), malaria is a febrile disease caused by parasite of the genus plasmodium and transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.
multiplication and develop to form liver schizonts which mature to form the merozoites (infective parasites). The merozoites leave the liver cells and enter the bloodstream again. Infected individuals may not exhibit sign and symptoms during this stage, which lasts between seven and thirty days.
Erythrocytic Stage
This is the period where the Red blood cells are invaded. The merozoites move into the bloodstream and invade the red blood cells. They multiply and are found in small segments called schizonts. They mature, rupture and release thousands of merozoites.
Epidemiology of Malaria
According to World Health Organization (2010), the disease mostly occurs in the tropical and sub-tropical regions particularly sub-Sahara Africa and South-East Asia. Malaria was wide spread in the 1880s in North America and other temperate regions in the world.
Each year, more than 300million cases of malaria are diagnosed and more than 1.5 million people die of the disease and prevalent in over 100 countries which include Ghana. Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent malaria parasite on the African continent.
One in five of the world’s population is at risk of malaria.
Each year, there are up to five hundred million deaths. More than 90% of these deaths are found in sub-Saharan Africa. It is also the leading cause of death in Ghana.
CAUSES
Malaria is cause by the plasmodium species. There are four different types of the parasite. These are:
Plasmodium ovale
Plasmodium malariae
Plasmodium falciparum
Plasmodium vivax
Plasmodium ovale are dormant forms and might produce clinical diseases 6 – 12 months after the initial infection.
Plasmodium malariae is usually associated with mild symptoms and bouts of fever every third day.
Plasmodium falciparum is the most dangerous type of the parasite and causes more severe complications. It is responsible for about 80% to 90% of the cases of the disease in Ghana.
Plasmodium vivax is a protozoal parasite and human pathogen. This parasite is the most frequent and widely distributed cause of recurring malaria
Mode Of Transmission
Malaria parasite can be transmitted through the following:
The bite of infected female anopheles’ mosquito
Transfusion of infected blood with the parasites
Pathophysiology Of Malaria
The pathophysiology of malaria deals with the disease process caused by the plasmodium parasite. This includes the life cycle of the plasmodium species. The development of the malaria parasite is divided into two distinct stages namely:
The asexual stage which is carried out in living beings specifically man.
The sexual stage which occurs in the female anopheles mosquito.
The Asexual Stage
This stage is divided into:
Pre-erythrocytic stage
Erythrocytic stage
Pre-Erythrocytic Stage
This is also referred to as period of incubation. When an infected female anopheles mosquito bites a human being, it introduces the plasmodium called the sporozoites into the victim’s blood. These sporozoites leave the bloodstream within half an hour and invade the liver cells, where the pre-erythrocytic stage begins. In the liver cells, the sporozoites undergo asexual. After the invasion of the red blood cells, the toxic product of the merozoites releases endogenous pyrogens from the leukocytes. These pyrogens act on the hypothalamus of the brain to release prostaglandins which acts on the posterior hypothalamus to stimulate the sympathetic nerves to contract blood vessels and decrease heat dissipation resulting in classical rigor. Majority of the merozoites enter the red blood cells to initiate another erythrocytic stage. Some of the merozoites develop into male and female gametocytes which are inert in human beings. It is this form which is transmitted from man through a bite to begin the sexual stage or cycle. The gametocytes die if no mosquito sucks them.
In the falciparum infection, the erythrocytic cycle takes 1 – 2 days, plasmodium vivax and ovaletake 2days and plasmodium malariae 3 days.
Phases Of Malaria
Malaria is usually present in three phases. These are:
First or Cold Phase: In this phase, the individual has raised body temperature. The temperature is normally above 37.5oc. The individual feels cold and shivers. The shivering results due to the body’s in-built mechanism to generate heat to maintain its normal temperature. Patient complains of itching, nausea, loss of appetite and experiences confusion. This stage lasts for about an hour.
Second or Hot Phase: During this stage, the patient feels hot, and complain of nausea, restlessness, headache and dizziness.
Third or Sweating Phase: The patient begins to sweat profusely. Temperature begins to return to normal (thus 36.6oc to 37.2oc). Patient feels weak and complains of excessive thirst and headache.
Clinical Features
The clinical features that are likely to be experienced include:
High fever (37.5oc – 40oc).
 Headache.
Nausea.
Vomiting.
Dizziness.
Malaise.
Profuse sweating.
Diarrhoea /constipation.
Bitterness in the mouth.
Fatigue.
Dark coloured urine.
 Convulsions in children.
 Abdominal pains.
 Joint pains.
Anorexia.
Complications
The following are common complications that usually occur with malaria:
Anemia
Splenomegaly
Cerebral malaria
Renal failure
Miscarriage/abortion in pregnancy liver failure
Black water fever
Diagnostic Investigations
Blood film for malaria parasite estimation
Full blood count
Blood analysis for haemoglobin estimation
Cardinal signs and symptoms
Treatment
Treatment of malaria is basically medical. Early treatment decreases the risk of developing complications such as anemia, cerebral malaria, renal failure and liver failure.
The following drugs may be prescribed for the treatment of malaria;
Artesunate-amodiaquine – this is the combination of two drugs developed to combat resistance of malaria parasite in human.
Analgesics and antipyretics are given to relieve pain and fever. For example, paracetamol.
Antiemetics are given in cases of nausea and vomiting. E.g., Promethazine (Phenergan), chlorpromazine (thorazine).
Vitamin supplements and folic acid are given. In extreme cases of anemia, blood transfusion is given.
Intravenous fluids / oral rehydration solution (ORS) are also given to replace loss fluids and to improve rehydration.
Nursing Care/Management
Rest, and Comfort
 Provide Complete bed rest would be provided for the patient in the phase of high temperature, malaise and anemia.
Position and changed often to prevent pressure sores.
For patient who are restless, bed with side rails or well-padded cot would be provided.
In situation of fever, tepid sponging would be provided for the patient

2.           Nutrition
Highly nutritious diet, high protein diet and calories would be given to the patient. Fruit juices such as orange, pineapple would also be served to the patient to enhance appetite.
Fluid intake (liberal) if patient can tolerate would be increased to improve hydration.
In children, nasogastric tube would be passed for weaker patients, to ensure adequate intake.
Food would be served in an attractive manner to boost patients’ appetite since there may be anorexia (loss of appetite).
Intravenous fluids would be provided in case of severe sweating, and dehydration.
Personal Hygiene
Patient would be encouraged to bath regularly or assisted if the need arises.
Soiled bed linen would be changed frequently and washed.
Personal clothing of the patient would be washed thoroughly when dirty.
Cleanliness of the hands and feet would be ensured.
oral care should be given at least twice daily
Observation
Temperature, pulse, respiration and blood pressure would be checked 4 hourly, but temperature would be monitored regularly.
Patient’s intake and output would be observed.
Signs of dehydration such as depressed fontanelles, sunken eyes in infants would be observed.
In case of blood transfusion or intravenous fluids (infusions), signs of circulatory overload, rate of flow and reactions would be observed.

Medications
Prescribed drugs would be served to the right patient, at the right time with the right dose, the right route, the right drug, the patient’s right to accept and reject the drug.
Patient would be observed for any reactions to medications.
Patient / Family would be educated on the desired and side effects of drug therapy.
 Psychological Support
The patient and family would be reassured to allay anxiety.
In children with convulsions, care givers or significant others find the situation very alarming, explanation would be offered to allay anxiety.
Patient and family would be encouraged to verbalize their fears and anxiety, to help clear out misconceptions and also to allay anxiety.

The patient and family would be educated and taught on the following preventive measures:
1. Pouring of oil on the surface of stagnant waters to kill mosquito larvae
2. Spraying surrounding bushes and waterlogs with insecticide.
3. Desilting choked gutters
4.Sleeping under treated mosquito nets.
5. Using trap door and nets at the windows in individual homes.
6.Application of mosquito repellant ointment on the skin.
7.Wearing of protective and long clothing especially during the night
8.Proper disposal of refuse and empty containers.

text:

text:
1.9 Literature Review On Gastritis
Gastritis is the inflammation of the stomach mucosal lining. It occurs when the stomach lining is been exposed to irritating substances such as medication, smoking, food allergies, or toxic chemicals.
Figure 1: Anatomy Of The Stomach

 Incidence
This condition is common among all ages especially adults and those who engage in alcoholism, smoking, ingestion of spicy food , and self-medication.

Types Of Gastritis
The two main types of gastritis are:
Acute Gastritis
Chronic Gastritis
Acute Gastritis
Acute gastritis is a benign and self-limiting inflammation of the gastric mucosa that is usually due to an exogenous substance that is the ingestion of an irritating substance. Endoscopic examination of the stomach of a person with acute gastritis reveals a reddened and oedematous gastric mucosa and possibly the presence of superficial erosion in the mucosa layer.
Causes of Acute Gastritis
Excess alcohol ingestion, drug effects, severe physical stress or trauma, ingestion of a caustic substance, radiation exposure, and bacterial contamination of food and water.
Aspirin
Chronic ingestion of irritating food such as pepper.
Alcohol ingestion
Chronic Gastritis
Chronic gastritis is inflammation of the stomach accompanied by disturbances in its secretory and motor function. Chronic gastritis can be a precursor of peptic ulcer and stomach cancer
Aetiology Of Chronic Gastritis
Exposure to irritating substances such as drugs, alcohol, cigarette, smoking, or environmental agents.
Occurs with pernicious anemia, renal diseases, or diabetes mellitus.
Bacterial infection with helicobacter pylori is a common cause of non-erosive chronic gastritis.
Aetiology/Causes Of Gastritis
Gastritis can result from any chemical, thermal, bacterial, or mechanical factors that injure the gastric mucosa.
Examples include:
Drugs such as aspirin, digitalis, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) alcohol and alcoholic beverages.
Excessive irritating food such as tea, coffee, pepper and other spicy foods those are hot or contaminated with staphylococcus.
Corrosive substances
Exposure to radiation
Immune disturbance
Endocrine disorders.
Pathophysiology
The mucosal lining of the stomach normally protects it from the action of gastric acid. If this barrier is penetrated by a bacterial infection, often helicobacter pylori, ingestion of corrosive, erosive infectious substances, certain types of radiation, gastritis will occur with resultant injury to the stomach mucosa. When hydrochloric acid comes into contact with the gastric mucosa, injury to the small vessels occur with oedema and sometimes haemorrhage and possible ulcer formation. The damage associated with acute gastritis is usually mild.
Following repeated attacks of acute gastritis, a progressive form develops, which is chronic gastritis. A destructive inflammatory change that begins on the surface of the mucus membrane extends to affect the whole membrane including the gastric glands. The mucosa of the stomach is thickened, and then the wall becomes thin resulting in lesser quantity and quality of secretions, eventually consisting of mucus and water only.

Diagnostic Investigations
A good history taking of clinical features reveals the disease.
Endoscopy reveals stomach lining inflammation and mucus erosion.
Serologic testing for antibodies against the H .pylori antigen.
Gastric analysis reveals high white blood cells count denotes a bacterial infection.
Stool examination
Gastroscopy.

Treatment
Intravenous fluids such as dextrose normal saline to replace fluid and electrolyte loss.
Iv metronidazole was administered to combat infection.
The treatment for corrosive gastritis was neutralized with intravenous omeprazole to relieve gastrointestinal.
Analgesics such as buscopan were given to relieve pain.
Nursing Management
Psychological Care
The patient was reassured that good treatment modalities have been put in place to help alleviate her abdominal pain and also patient was introduced to other patients who are successfully recovering from gastritis.
Rest And Sleep.
Rest and sleep should be ensured to conserve energy and relax patients. The patient should be nursed in a comfortable position. Preferably supine position to reduce pain. Ensure good ventilation in the ward to promote comfort and rest.
Nutrition
The bland diet was served to avoid irritation of the gastric mucosa and abdominal pain. The patient was also advised to stop eating spicy foods, too much pepper too, hot and cold food to avoid irritation of the gastric mucosa.
Personal Hygiene
The patient was given an assisted bath twice daily. Hair was dried to keep the patient fresh. Her mouth cared for twice daily with brush and toothpaste containing fluoride to maintain freshness and also prevent oral infection such as gingivitis. Her toes and fingernails were cared for to prevent them from harbouring microbes. Her linen were changed when soaked or soiled with body fluids. All these were done to prevent infections, promote good personal hygiene, and enhances patient comfort.
Observation
Vital signs such as temperature, pulse, respiration were closely monitored and recorded 4hourly. This will help the nurse to know if there is any deviation from normal which needs to be corrected to prevent complications.
Fluid intake and output were maintained, the patient’s level of consciousness which is an orientation to time, place, person, as well as a side effect of drugs, were observed. The patient’s skin was checked for signs of dehydration and anaemia.
The colour of Vomitus was also observed for any abnormality. The patient’s level of pain was assessed. The abdomen was also examined for distension.
Education
Education was done to give patient insight into her condition. The patient was educated that gastritis occurs when there is inflammation of gastric mucosa, thus the layer that lines the stomach and it can be caused by drugs such as aspirin, corrosive substances, excessive irritating foods such as tea smoking, eating spicy food and other sedentary lifestyle .
Some of the signs and symptoms include  epigastric pain, abdominal cramping, vomiting, and fever. The patient was educated to adhere strictly to the nutrition required to ensure a quick recovery. She was advised to avoid food and beverages that are irritating to the stomach lining such as coffee and alcohol.
Medication
The patient was served with antibiotics to prevent infections; analgesics were served to control patient pain. Antiemetics were administered to control vomiting, intravenous fluid such as Dextrose Normal saline was served to prevent dehydration and intravenous omeprazole to neutralized gastric acid.
All measures were ensured to make sure patient drugs were taking without problems.
The drugs served were recorded in the drug administration chart and the desired and side effect observed and recorded in the nurse’s notes.
Validation Of Data
The patient’s history, clinical manifestation, and assessment confirmed that the patient was suffering from gastritis. When data collected were compared with the literature review, it was clear that the patient was suffering from gastritis. This proved that all the data and information gathered were valid and free from errors and biases.

The patient was made to assume left side lateral positions to help reduce abdominal pain supporting the head with a pillow on the prepared admission bed. Cold compress was applied to the patient head and 1gram of Paracetamol was administered to reduce the headache. Patient Intravenous line was secured. The patient was infused with Dextrose Normal Saline 500mls and a sample of blood and urine were taken for laboratory investigations.
The Doctor diagnosed her of Gastritis. The patient prescribed medications were administered.  Mrs. M.A was reassured of competent healthcare team and speedy recovery. Patient relatives were oriented to the ward. They were also informed about the hospital’s policies on visiting hours, ward rules, the items needed during hospitalization. Patient relatives were allowed to bid her farewell as they left for the house. Patient information collected were written and documented in the Admission and Discharge book.
On the day of admission, the patient complained of abdominal pain. A goal was set up at 9:30 am  to relieved pain within 24hours. The goal was fully met on 16th November,2022 at 9:30 am.
On this same day, the patient complained of headache, an objective was set at 11:30 am to reduce patients’ headache within 4 hours; this was met by patient verbalizing that there is relief of headache and the nurse observing patient having a cheerful facial expression at 3:30 pm on the 15th November 2022.
On the same day, the patient had a fever, an objective was set at 1:30 am to reduce patient body temperature within 4hours; this was met as nurse checking patient temperature  and recording normal value ( 36.6degree Celsius) at 5;30pm on 15th November, 2022
On the same day, an objective was set at 3:30 pm to maintain patient adequate body fluid and electrolyte within 4 hours; this was met as nurse observed patient and was no longer vomiting at 7:30 pm on the 15th of November, 2022.
First Day Of Admission (16th November, 2022)
The patient woke up around 6:00am patient slept well as evidenced by the night nurse. Brushed her teeth, took her bath and was served with her breakfast which was porridge and bread. Mrs. M.A’s daughter was reassured that the patient was in the hands of competent healthcare team who will put appropriate measures in place to solve her problem. During the ward rounds, patient complained of abdominal pain. The patient’s prescribed drugs were administered. The patient complained of abdominal pain on the same day of admission. The patient was reassured on measures put in place to relieve pain. The patient was assisted to assume a prone to relieve pain. Cold compresses were applied to the epigastrium to relieve pain at 10:30 am.
The patient was advised not to take caffeinated drinks and spicy food since it can cause high production of hydrochloric acid in the stomach which will result in mucosa irritation.  Infusion dextrose normal saline 500mls was set up, regulated to the required drops per minute, and recorded.
During the afternoon, Mrs. M.A was made to walk around in the ward for 15minutes after which she took her sleep. Upon awakening, she was given a cup of water to rinse the mouth and was served with rice and stew on a plate in which she ate a quarter of the food. Due medications were administered. Mrs. M.A then engaged in a conversation with her ward mates.
Around 4:30 pm, her daughter and sister came for visit. They talked for a while and the patient was happy. I informed them of my intention to visit their house the following day which they agreed.
The patient was assisted to have a warm bath after which she was served fufu and light soup at 5:00 pm. She ate half of the fufu. Due medications were administered and documented and she slept around 8:30 pm.
The day's range of vital signs was checked and recorded as follows:
Temperature                  36.4 - 36.7 degree Celsius
Pulse                              80 - 90 beats per minutes
Respiration                      20 - 22 cycle per minutes
Blood pressure                    100/75 - 110 - 80 millimeter of mercury

Second Day of Admission (17th November, 2022)
The patient woke up around 5:30am. According to the night nurse, patient slept well in the night without any complains. In the morning patient looked well and healthy and maintained her hygiene without assistance. The patient took porridge and slices of bread for her breakfast. She said the intensity of her abdominal pain has reduced. The Doctor came and reviewed the patient and asked that previous medications should be continued. The patient was advised not to starve herself since this can worsen her condition.
During the afternoon, around 12:30pm, the patient was served with banku and okro stew. She was engaged in watching television to divert her attention from the pain. Prescribed medications administered. A comfortable bed free from creases and cramps was prepared for the patient to improve the patient sleep pattern. Ward noise was minimized and ventilation was provided by opening nearby windows and switching on fans.
The patient was encouraged to take a warm bath in the evening after which she was served with Rice and Stew.  She ate 2/3 of the food served.
The day’s range of vital signs were checked and recorded as:
Temperature               36.1 - 37.0 degree Celsius
Pulse                            86 - 95 beat per minute
Respiration                 22 - 24 cycle per minute
Blood pressure         116/80 - 120/85 millimeter of mercury.
Third-Day of Admission (18th November, 2022)
Mrs. M.A woke up and she looked cheerful. She attended to her hygiene without assistance according to the night nurse. The patient took her breakfast Hausa porridge with bread. The Doctor came and review her and also planned for possible discharge the next day since her condition was stable. The patient and family lacked knowledge on the causes, signs, and symptoms and treatment regimens of gastritis. Health education was given on the causes, signs and symptoms, treatment regimen of gastritis, and the prevention of gastritis. Patient due medications were administered as prescribed. She took her sleep. Upon awakening, she was given a cup of water to rinse the mouth and was served with rice and stew on a plate which she ate half of the food. Due medications were administered. The day vitals were checked and recorded as
Temperature- 36.2 - 36.4 degree Celsius
Pulse -70 - 82 beats per minute,
Respiration- 24-26 cycle per minute
Blood pressure – 117/75- 120/78 millimeters of mercury

Day Of Discharge (19th November, 2022)
The patient woke up around 6:00am and was seen on this day looking very cheerful interacting with patients on the ward. She has already attended to her hygiene. According to the night staff nurses, she slept peacefully throughout the night. she had no complains. She took Oat with slices of bread. During the ward rounds, the Physician Assistant saw her improvement and the Physician made a discharge and set a review date in a week.

The day’s vital signs were checked and recorded as follows;
Temperature                  36.2degree Celsius
Pulse                                80 beat per minute
Respiration                     20 cycle per minute
Blood pressure 110/70 Millimetre of mercury
The patient was discharged home on the following medications,
Tablet metronidazole 400mg tds x 7 days
Tab Cefuroxime 500mg bd ×7days
Cap omeprazole 20mg bd ×14days
Syrup nugel O 15mls tds ×7days
She was informed as to when to come for review. This was on the 26th of November, 2022. Mrs. M.A was educated on how to take the drugs, their actions, and side effects, she was advised to report on any sign reoccurring or complications to the hospital for necessary treatment. She was advised on dietary modification, reduction of stress, maintenance of good personal hygiene, avoidance of the intake of mucosal irritants such as spices, alcohol, and the intake of over the counter drugs. She was made aware of the need for home visits. Mrs. M A and daughter expressed their sincere gratitude to all the healthcare team on duty, for the care and attention during her period of attention.
She was helped to pack her belongings and escorted her and the daughter to the roadside and bid them goodbye. Bed linings, pillows, mattresses and bedside lockers were disinfected. Documentation was done in the admission and discharge book as well as ward state.
Preparation Of Patient For Discharge And Rehabilitation
Preparation of Mrs. M. A for discharge and rehabilitation started on the day of admission which was 15th November, 2022 to give patient and family insight into her condition which included the cause, signs and symptoms, complications, prevention of disease and the need to report to the hospital early when there is any detection of any bad sign of an illness. This was done to ensure that, care could also be given to the patient in the house. On 18th November, 2022 around 9:00am, the Doctor came on ward rounds and reviewed Mrs. M.A for discharge on the next day. The patient was informed about the discharge.  She started packing her things. The patient was educated not to engage in strenuous exercise, have enough rest, and a well balanced diet which should be spice - free and also void when the urge comes. She was also educated not to take over- the- counter drugs, caffeinated drinks and alcohol. The patient was educated on how to take her medications, time, dosage, storage and side effects of the medications.
The patient was educated on the need to maintain good personal hygiene such as care of the mouth, bathing, care of hands, and feet. The patient and family were also informed about the need to keep cooking utensils, sources of water and food clean, and proper disposal of dry and wet refuse to help prevent the occurrence of communicable diseases. On the day before discharge, patient and family were informed about the discharge as her condition was stable and the estimation on her hospital bill was made known to her family members, she was also informed that, even though she was on health insurance scheme, some drugs and labs were not covered by the NHIS so financial preparation was necessary. The patient was finally discharged home on 19th November 2022 and was asked to come for review on 26th November, 2022.

Follow Up/Home Visit/Continuity of Care
This comprises visits made to the home of the patient to familiarize yourself with the environment and look out for potential and actual problems that interfere with the health of the patient.
This visit also helps to acquire the health, environment, and socio-economic conditions of the patient and her family and helps to ensure continuity of care.
First Home Visit (17th November, 2022)
Before discharge, a home visit was embarked on to assess the patient's home environment which formed the basis of patient and family education. The first visit to Mrs. M.A's home was on 17th November, 2022 which happened to be her second day on admission. The visit was taken place at Adomakokrom accompanied by  her daughter after she came to visit her mother in the afternoon.
On arrival, a seat and water were offer and I was given a warmly reception after which two boys were introduced as neighbors. The purpose of the home visit was explained to the daughter and sister to help the nurse assess their home situation. To also find factors that might have contributed to the patient’s condition and to interact with them concerning their health with their environment and lifestyle.
The daughter and sister of Mrs. M.A were educated on how to maintain food, environmental and personal hygiene, the significance   of taking a healthy balanced diet, regular exercise, and how to care for Mrs. M.A who was on admission.
After the education, they were informed of the next visit which would be after the discharge of the patient. Permission was asked to leave. Mrs. M.A’s relatives expressed their appreciation, gratitude and farewell messages were exchanged.
Second Home Visit (22rd September, 2022)
The second home visit was made on 22rd November, 2022 after the patient was discharged. The visit was aimed at knowing how the patient was responding to treatment and her adherence to the treatment regimen. The visit was to remind them about the date of review which was on 26th November, 2022  and also verify if education given was implemented.
On arrival, I received a warmly reception from the patient and her family. They were able to give correct feedback on all the previous education given to them which was aimed at improving their health conditions. Patient drugs were inspected and it was confirmed that,patient adhered strictly to all her prescribed medications and treatment regimen. It was made clear to them that the next home visit will be the last visit and my intention to hand over patient to the family for continuity of care during the next visit but the family was unhappy so an explanation was made to them for deeper understanding and bid them goodbye.
Review Day on The 26th of November, 2022.
On 26th November, 2022 the day of review, Mrs. M.A and her daughter were met at the Out-Patient Department(OPD) at 7:45am.  We exchanged greetings and warmly welcomed them. Her folder was collected from the records office and sent to the nurse at OPD. Vital signs checked and recorded;
Temperature 36.5 degree Celsius
Pulse 80 beats per minute
Respiration 130/90 millimeters of mercury
The patient was reviewed by a Physician, patient lodged no complains saying that she was feeling better. She was advised to take the medications as prescribed. The patient and her daughter were reminded about my next home visit. They were accompanied to the entrance of the hospital and  bit them goodbye.
Third Home Visit 9th December, 2022
On the said date, a first home visit was carried out to know how the patient's health has improved and to terminate care. The patient and her relatives gave me warm reception on my arrival was , greetings were exchanged and the health of the patient was assessed.
The patient had recovered fully and confirmed that she no longer feels headache, abdominal pain, feverish, no longer feels nausea and vomiting. The patient and family also demonstrated a clear understanding of the need and how to properly administer medications at home.
The patient and family were further educated on the need to report immediately to the hospital upon recognition of any adverse effects of the drugs or change in their health. They were also encouraged to report to the hospital regularly for medical review. Previous education is given on hygiene, a balanced diet, and others were reemphasized. Though it was difficult task patting company with them, I did all my best and made them aware that I am just ending the interaction officially but I am always at their service when the need arises. Finally, they were informed that care rendered to Mrs. M.A and the family have been terminated but nurse Agyeiwaa Evelyn who is a community health nurse will ensure continuity of care. They expressed their gratitude and appreciation about the knowledge acquired, I thanked them for their cooperation and soughted permission to leave.

chapter: Chapter Five: Evaluation Of Care Rendered To The Patient /Family
heading: Introduction
text:
Evaluation is the final stage of the nursing process and it is done to know whether goals set were met fully, partially met, or unmet at all, and if not, the action to be taken to meet the objectives set.
Statement of Evaluation
After Mrs. M.A had been on admission for four days, her condition improved and she was discharged home on 19th November, 2022. This was possible because all goals and objectives set were fully met while the patient was on admission.
15th November, 2022
An objective was set up at 9:30am to relieve abdominal pain within 24hours, the goal was fully met as patient verbalised that the pain has reduced   and  nurse observing that patient is having  cheerful facial expression on 16/11/2022 at 9:30am
An objective was set at 11:30am to reduce patients’ headache within 4 hours; this was met by patient verbalizing there is no more  headache   and nurse observing that patient is having cheerful facial expression on the 15th November, 2022 at 3:30pm
An objective was set at 1:30pm to reduce patient body temperature within 4hours; this was met as nurse checking patient temperature and it has reduced to the normal range ( 36.6 degrees Celsius) on 15th November, 2022 at 5:30pm.
An objective was set 3:30pm to maintain patient adequate body fluid and electrolyte within 4 hours; this was met as nurse observed that patient  was no longer vomiting at 7:30pm on the 15th of November, 2022.
16th November, 2022
An objective was set at 10:am to help reduce abdominal pain by assuming the prone position and applying cold compress on the epigastric region within 2hours . Goal was fully met as patient verbalized the pain has subsided and nurse observed that   patient was  having cheerful facial expression  on 16th November, 2022 at 12:00pm.
18th November, 2022
An objective was set at 12˸pm to help the patient and family gain insight into Gastritis throughout hospitalization. The objective was fully met on 18th November, 2022 at 2:00pm as patient verbalized that she understands her condition and nurse observed that patient was able to answer questions on the causes, signs and symptoms, treatment regimen and prevention of gastritis correctly.
19th November, 2022
Education was done on how to take the drugs, their actions, and side effects, she was advised to report any sign reoccurrence or complications to the hospital for necessary treatment. She was advised on dietary modification, reduction of stress, maintenance of good personal hygiene, avoidance of the intake of mucosal irritants such as spices, alcohol, and the intake of over the counter drugs.
Amendment of Nursing Care
Due to the nature of the quality and holistic care given with the help of the patient and her family together with good healthcare team , all objectives set were fully met. However, no amendment of care was done
Termination of Care
This marks the end of interaction between the nurse and the patient. The interaction with the patient and family started on 15th November, 2022 till the last home visit which was on 9th December, 2022. To prevent separation of anxiety, it was made clear to the patient and family that our interaction was therapeutic one which will last for only a short period.
They were educated on the maintenance of good personal and environmental hygiene, nutrition, and adherence to the treatment regimen, stress management as well as the need for follow up care.
Finally, the patient’s care was terminated on 9th December, 2022. Due to the earlier attempt made to prepare patients for realities of separation, no ill effects were recognized after care was terminated.

SUMMARY
Mrs. M.A a 94-year-old woman was admitted to the female's medical ward at Goaso Municipal Hospital on 15th November, 2022. She was diagnosed of Gastritis. She was taken through a series of investigations which included the Malaria Parasite test, Full Blood Count, Helicobacter Pylori test, Urine for Routine Examination. The result of investigations and signs and symptoms helped confirm her diagnosis. The patient presented health problems such as abdominal pain, headache, fever, nausea, and Vomiting.
Objectives were set and orders implemented, which include monitoring of vital signs, reassuring patient, assessing the patient level of pain tepid sponging, and administration of medications were carried out successfully.
The patient and family were educated on the causes, signs and symptoms, management, prevention and complications of Gastritis. Also, they were advised to take drug regiment very serious and accordingly. Mrs. M.A responded positively to treatment and condition improved.
The patient was nursed for four days from 15th November, 2022 to 19th November, 2022 and was discharged. She was due for review on 26th November, 2022. Follow-ups and home visits were made to assess the home situation and observed the drug and treatment regimen. This was when the patient's care was finally terminated.








CONCLUSION
This study has affirmed the need and importance of comprehensive nursing of the patient and their families. The care study has been a significant benefit to me since it has broadened and enlightened my knowledge of gastritis, its signs and symptoms, causes, diagnosis,prevention and its treatment. It has also helped me to bring out the knowledge acquired in the various subjects in my three years training and helped me to know how to establish a good rapport with patient and family as well as good nurse and patient relationship.

heading: Preamble
text:
MyPREFACE
The patient/family care study forms part of the assessment of every final year student as required by the Nurses and Midwife council of Ghana. It is required of every candidate in order to fulfil the award of Diploma in Registered General Nursing. The patient/family care study is a comprehensive account of all nursing care rendered to the patient and family from the day of admission until the day of discharge and it covers follow up visits.
This study usually helps the student to apply the changing trend in nursing in the care of the patient. Nursing in the olden days were focussed towards disease and illness, but today there is increasing recognition of people’s need for health care as distinct from illness care.
Also nursing practice was based on intuitive or observations or based on observations or experiences; however, the past two decades have brought emphasis on nursing research and the use of scientific data at the bedside.
Nurses continue to gain autonomy and respect as members of the health care team as they are depending on their professional body of knowledge, which was not done in the past.
Today, it is the duty of the nurse to device methods to help meet the needs of the client, as a team player (health care team). Approaches used in nursing today is called nursing process which can be achieved through functional team or care nursing. Nursing today, has also evolved to the level of use of computers for effectiveness and efficiency and to reduce the workload of nurses. The care study helps to upgrade the standards of nursing through competency and rendering of individualised and holistic care to clients.
The improvement of interpersonal relationship between the student nurse and patient as well as with other health professionals cannot be over looked as an advantage of this study. In addition, it helps the student nurse to put into practice his/her learned theories and acquire more information in order to help him/her render a comprehensive and holistic care, taking into consideration the family needs also. All these reason and many other necessitated the need for this study as a requirement by the Nurses and Midwives Council of Ghana.



















ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
My sincere gratitude goes to the Almighty Allah for granting me wisdom, knowledge, guidance and protection throughout this study.
I would also like to express my gratitude to my client Madam P.D  and her  family for their support and consent to interact with me and allowing me to put my knowledge into practice.
I wish to express my deepest appreciation to the medical director, nursing administrator, the-ward -in-charge of female's ward, the ward doctors and staff of the ward through whose support and guidance this work has become a success.
To the tutorial staff and non-teaching staff of seikwa nursing and midwifery training college for their guidance, corrections and patience and time to make this work what it is. All that I would like to say is that, may almighty Allah richly bless them all.
Last but not the least, my thanks go to my family, my former headmaster, Mr O.A at the emergency unit Methodist Hospital Wenchi, my room -mates, my loved ones (Diploma 2 and 3) and my classmates (Diploma1) all at Methodist University College Ghana-Department of Nursing, for their support in making this study a reality. May the almighty God, bless you all.






INTRODUCTION
The study was conducted on Mr. A.A. a 30-year-old man who was admitted at Methodist Hospital Wenchi, on the 20th September, 2016 with the diagnosis of Acute Appendicitis. Ultrasound scan was used to confirm his diagnosis. Haemoglobin level estimation was done.
The patient presented the following health problems; anxiousness, pains at the incisional site and insomnia. These problems were taken care of, using the nursing process as a guide. Due to client adherence to treatment given, he responded well to the treatment prescribed and was discharged on the 24th September, 2016 without any complication.
To ensure smooth continuity of care three home visits were also made to assess the patient’s condition before and after discharge. The interaction with Mr. A.A.and her family, started on the 20th September, 2016 being the day of admission through to 24th September, 2016, the day of discharge and termination of care on the 20th of November, 2016. Some of the nursing care rendered to my client to help solve his problems included, reassurance, heath education, wound dressing, and other personal hygiene needs, among other. He was treated with analgesic; tramadol, Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like Diclofenac to manage pain, antibiotics like Metronidazole, Amoksiclav, were served as ordered to prevent occurrence of infection after the surgery while intravenous fluid like normal saline, ringers lactate and dextrose saline were also served to maintain hydration, maintain fluid and electrolyte balance. On the day of discharge, client’s condition had improved remarkably without any complications.
The report of the study has been divided into six (6) chapters as follows;
Chapter one (1) covers the assessment of patient/ family.
chapter two (2) also talks about analysis of data collected.
chapter three (3) entails planning for patient/family care.
chapter four (4) focuses on the implementation of patient/family care plan.
chapter five (5) deals with evaluation of care rendered to the patient/family.
chapter six (6) deals with summary and conclusions.

chapter: Chapter One: 1.0Assessment Of The Patient / Family
heading: Introduction
text:
INTRODUCTION
Assessment is the first step in the nursing process and it is the beginning of the nursing care to the patient and family. It gives information about the patient, her family and her  community. During the assessment phase, all these pieces of information are gathered gradually, starting from the day of admission. The data collected from the client would enable the nurse to give a holistic nursing care, using the appropriate nursing care plan for the client, his/her family and the community in which he/she lives.

chapter: Chapter One: 1.0Assessment Of The Patient / Family
heading: 1.1 PATIENT'S PARTICULARS

1.1 PATIENT’S PARTICULARS
