1.9LITERATURE REVIEW ON APPENDICITIS
DEFINITION
Appendicitis is the inflammation of the vermiform appendix; it often occurs when the appendix become inflamed from ulceration of the mucosa or obstruction of the appendiceal lumen.
INCIDENCE
Appendicitis may occur at any age but it is rare in under 2 years and uncommon between 2 and 4 years.  Usually, children over 4 years of age are mostly affected and males are at higher risk than females.  The disease is more prevalent in countries in which people consume low fibre diet and high carbohydrate diets.
TYPES OF APPENDICITIS
1.
        1  Acute appendicitis
2.   Sub-acute appendicitis
3.   Chronic appendicitis.


Acute appendicitis
This is sudden on onset and occurs within few hours or days and may go on to suppuration.
Sub – acute appendicitis
In this, the mucosa and the sub mucosa are inflamed and oedematous and the appendix may be swollen and the serosa red with increased vascularity.  If untreated, resolution occurs but with formation of fibrous adhesions either within the lumen or on the serosa forming a kink.  This may obstruct the lumen and may cause a much more severe pain.
Chronic appendicitis
This type has a gradual onset and recurrent episodes which may be due to obstruction from adhesions and endoluminal obstructions. It may also arise as a result of gradual hyperplasia of the lymphoid tissues.
AETIOLOGY OF ACUTE APPENDICITIS
The main cause of appendicitis is unknown.  However it can be attributed to the following predisposing factors;
I. Bacterial Infection
- Escherichia coli
- Streptococcal organisms
II. Obstructions
Foreign body
Faecolith
Hyperplasia of lymphoid tissue
Adhesions
Intestinal parasites such as round worms and pin worm infestations.
PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
The appendix become inflamed and edematous as a result of becoming kinked or occluded by fecalith (ie, hardened mass of stool),tumor or foreign body.The inflammatory process increase intraluminal pressure, initiating a progressively severe , generalized,or periumbilical pain that becomes localized to the right lower quadrant of the abdomen within a few hours.Eventually, the inflamed appendix fills with pus.Once obstructed, the appendix become ischemic, becteria overgrowth occurs, and eventually gangrene occurs ( Brunner and surdarth textbook of medical surgical nursing 13 edition).



DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS
Acute appendicitis may be confused with a large number of diseases, there are wide spectrum of potential differential diagnosis for suspected  cause of appenditis which are;
1. Gynacological - overian cyst rapture, etopic pregnancy pelvic inflammatory disease.
2. Renal - ureteric stones, urinary tract infestion, phylonephritis.
3. Gestrointestinal - inflammatory bowl disease Meckel's diverticulum,or diverticolar disease.
4. Urological- testicular tortion, epididymo-orchitis.
Specifically in children, differential diagnosis to consider include mesenteric adenitis, gastroenteritis, constipation, intussusception or urinary tract infestion.(TeachMe surgery.(2023,June 26) acute appendicitis.Retrieved from http://teachmesurgery .com/general/large/appenditis).
CLINICAL FEATURES OF APPENDICITIS
Sudden severe or acute abdominal pain (colicky, cramping)
Nausea and vomiting. Profuse in high obstruction and none in low obstruction.  (vomiting first colourless or greenish then becomes light brown, dark brown in late stages due to intestinal contents)
Low grade fever (37ºC)
Localised tenderness at the McBurney’s point
Diarrhoea or constipation
Abdominal muscle guarding; the area is tender on palpation and becoming rigid gradually.
Positive Rovsing’s signs:  pressure in the left iliac fossa causes pain in the lower right iliac fossa.
urgency of micturation (if the appendix impinges on the urinary bladder).



COMPLICATIONS OF ACUTE APPENDICITIS
Perforation of the appendix (the rupturing of the appendix)
Peritonitis -becteria can cause inflammation of the abdomenal lining, which can be fetal.
Spread of infection -The infection can travel through the bloodstream and infect other organs.

Abscess (collection of pus in the appendix.

Septicaemia (infection of the blood). (Kennan,Sneha(2019,may 08 APPENDICITIS icliniq.retrieved from http//:www.icliniq.com.






DIAGNOSTIC INVESTIGATIONS
Personal medical history
Physical examination by palpation of abdomen
Observation of clinical features presented by client example positive Rovsing’s sign.
Laboratory examinations
White blood cell count:  there is a slight increase above 10,000/mm³ in 80% of all cases
Neutrophils increase above 75% in 89% of all cases
Haemoglobin level estimation which may be low
Urinalysis may reveal occult haematuria
Radiological examinations
Abdominal x-ray may detect the Faecalith that may be the cause of the disease as in children.
Abdominal ultrasound may be done to detect one enlarged appendix or abscess especially in females to rule out conditions of the ovaries, fallopian tubes etc that can mimic appendicitis.
NURSING MANAGEMENT
PERSONAL HYGIENE/REDUCING INFECTION.
-The patient’s personal hygiene should be maintained. Patient is assisted and encouraged to take care of the body (bathing), toe and finger nails, the hair and his clothing.
Personal oral hygiene is maintained by ensuring that patient’s teeth is brushed twice each day. Bed linen and clothing are also kept clean. Also patient’s elimination needs are met by offering bed pan or urinal each time patient asks for it. After elimination, patient’s perineal area is cleaned with a toilet roll then cleaned with water and soap; this is done to prevent infection of the perineal region.
- intravenous antibiotics administrator as prescribe by the the physician to prevent infection.
NUTRITION
- Patient was educated on food that she should and those she shouldn't eat e.g eating food that contains fiber,food should be chewed well before swollen, patient was educated good hygiene to prevent becteria infection and making sure her food always free from food particles like seeds and the likes.
- plan diet with patient, encouraged oral care to boost appetite in order for her to eat well.

C.  REDUCING PAIN
Is important that the patient has a calm peaceful rest and sleep to relax the muscle a nurse makes sure he or she provide comfortable bed and soft pillows , good ventilation and a quiet environment as well, so that patient can relax well.divertional therapy was given to relieve of pain  by  watching TV  which make the patient a little bit relax . Application of warm compress to the affect area(abdomen)so that pain can be reduce. Changing of position and preventing fatigue also help in reducing pain.The nurse may also serve the patient with a warm beverage. Sedative and analgesic may be served for the purpose of rest and relieved of pain if the above mentioned measures fail.
D. ELIMINATION  FLUID VOLUME DEFICIT
patient need to be hydrated.
- The nurse Keeps an accurate record of oral fluid and maintain a record of output (ie urine, liquid, stool, vomitus )
-The nurse monitor daily weight for fluid volume deficit (ie dry skin, mucous membrane, decrease in skin turgor and oliguria).
-The nurse encouraged oral fluid intake and monitor the flow of iv infusion and measure to decrease diarrheal (antidiarrheal agent).

E. OBSERVATION
- Patient vitals was  monitored which were   temperature, pulse, respiration and blood pressure,spo2 and glocose level every 4hourly until patient’s condition stabilizes.
 - The site of infusion is checked for swelling, needle dislodgementand cleaning the site of infusion to prevent infection.upon observation  patient was not looking pale,well hydrated and she has no physical impairment like hearing loss etc.and monitor side effects of the medication as well therapeutic effect too.
- Pain assessment is also done, this is achieved by assessing for restlessness and facial expression. The location, intensity and type of pain is assessed. If pain is caused by position, change the patient’s position gently to enhance her comfort and not contraindicated to her condition.
- The patient’s level of consciousness is assessed to see if she is fully conscious or deeply unconscious. This can be done by pricking or calling her  by her  name or using a torch light to assess whether the pupil reacts to light or not. Patient mental orientation is observed as time goes on.
F. REDUCING ANXIETY
-patient was  reassured of she being the hands  of  competent nurses,she will fine as her health is concerned.
-Teach patient proper management of relieving stress.
- By encouraging patient to practice deep breathing exercise so she will be relieved off the strees.(Brunner and surdarth textbook surgically medical nursing 13th edition.)
PREVENTION OF APPENDICITIS
The following measures should be observed in the prevention of appendicitis
Health Education. The general public should be educated to report at the hospital with sudden, acute abdominal pain and other illness promptly.
There should be education on good and environmental hygiene (prevent Amoebic, worm infestations)
Periodic medical examination should be encouraged
Eating of high fibre diet and adequate fluid intake to prevent the formation of Faecolith.
The general public should be taught the basic clinical features of appendicitis such as peri-umbilical pain accompanied by anorexia, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea or constipation.
Person  with such clinical presentation can either be manage both surgically and medically.

heading: Introduction
text:
Planning is a systematic approach to patient care, in which the nurse together with the patient and relatives identify the problems of the patients, set realistic goals and objectives for patient care and identify patient strength that will help facilitate the process.
Based on the problems and strengths identified, are suitable nursing orders and interventions made and implemented. At the end of the implementation an evaluation is done to assess whether the set objectives were achieved or not.
Planning is also priority-based and depending on the patient’s condition the set goal can either be long or short termed.

text:
4.1 SUMMARY OF ACTUAL NURSING CARE
The summary of the actual nursing care rendered to client during the period of admission include the following.
DAY OF ADMISSION (20th October, 2016)
My client was met at the OPD at 10:15am. I read through his folder and got to know he was to be admitted at the male’s ward which I led him to. The ward in-charge told me to make him comfortable in a bed at the private ward. At the ward, patient and his relative were welcomed warmly and made him comfortable in a seat at the nurses’ station. I read through his folder again, I called him by name which he responded and I welcomed him once more. I introduced myself as a final year student of the Methodist University College Ghana-Department of Nursing who wanted to take him as client and give to him total nursing care till he is discharged home and continue thereafter. I then introduced him to the ward in-charge and other staff and took him to his bed side. Vital signs were done and recorded as;
 Temperature………….38.7oC
Pulse…………………..64bpm
Respiration……………19bpm
Blood Pressure……….123/76mmHg
Weight………………...94Kg
The patient’s particulars were then entered into the admission and discharge book and the daily ward bed state.
The patient and family were orientated to the ward, with the ward routines adequately explained to them. Patient and family valuables were properly stored.
Patient and family were reassured and the client was then made comfortable in bed.
He was made to understand that he was not to be given food for the next 24hours because of the surgery the next day, with emphasis made on the importance of the surgery to his health.
SECOND DAYOFADMISSION (21ST October, 2016).
On the second day of admission, client woke up at 5: 30am, He was assisted to take his bath and also assisted to care for the mouth by brushing his teeth. His vital signs were checked and recorded. Allprescribed medications were served as ordered. The skin from the umbilicus down the lower abdomen was prepared by shaving, cleaned with savlon and covered with a sterile towel. He was also changed into a theatre gown. Client’s vital signs were checked and recorded as follows;
Temperature		37.10c,
Pulse			68bpm,
Respiration		16bpm
Blood pressure	160/90mmHg.
The consent form was explained to client which he agreed to sign appropriately. All laboratory investigation results were attached to patient’s folder. Client was made comfortable in bed.



PRE-OPERATIVE MANAGEMENT
Client was urgently prepared for appendicectomy under the following headings;
Psychological Preparation.
Physical Preparation.
Physiological Preparation.
Spiritual Preparation.
Socio-Economic Preparation.
PSYCHOLOGICAL PREPARATION
Client and family were reassured that the surgery was going to be successful. They were assured to allay fear or anxiety. The expected outcome of the surgery was also explained to them. He was also made aware of the post-operative pain, but told that analgesics will be given to take care of the pain. The client was taken through the consent form and made to sign as required by the hospital.
Client was told about what to expect in the theatre; the staff dressed in theatre gowns, face mask etc. He was also informed that he would be put to sleep prior to the operation by injection. He was also informed about the different theatre environment including sophisticated machines. Example the cardiac monitors etc.
PHYSICAL PREPARATION
Observation
Client’s vital signs (that is temperature, pulse, respiration) and blood pressure were continuously observed. Intravenous infusions which were administered were monitored to prevent fluid overload as well as leakages.

Personal Hygiene
Client’s personal hygiene was maintained. He was encouraged and assisted to take care of his body (bathing), toe and finger nails, hair and his clothing. Patient was assisted to bath twice in a day with mild soap and sponge; he was then groomed in bed. Client also had his teeth brushed twice in a day; bed linens were changed all the time with clean ones.
Nutrition
Client was put on Nil per OS, however, intravenous fluids were administered. Patient wasreassured of resuming feeding after the surgery and when indicated by the physician. The importance of maintaining nil per OS was explained to patient as this was to prevent post-operative complications such as aspiration.
Exercise
Post-operative exercises such as deep breathing, coughing and leg exercises were demonstrated to patient. It was further explained to patient that, there exercises will be performed regularly during the post-operative period to avoid any complications and to improve his well-being, physical comfort and safety. The importance of early ambulation was encouraged and explained to patient as it promotes quick recovery.
Rest and Sleep
Client was encouraged and assisted to have a calm peaceful rest the night before surgery. To ensure this, a comfortable bed with soft pillows were provided. Also, client was nursed in a quiet environment and then assisted to have a warm bath to enhance circulation and refresh him. A loose fitting pyjamas was given to patient to enhance comfortability.


Skin Preparation
The purpose of skin preparation was to reduce the incidence of wound infection and this was done on the morning of the day of operation. Client was screened and area was cleansed with soapy solution, then it was shaved carefully. After shaving, the area was thoroughly cleaned with soapy water. The area was the dried, covered with a sterile towel and secured in position.
PHYSIOLOGICAL PREPARATION
The laboratory examination; haemoglobin level estimation and blood for grouping and cross –matching were collected and shown to the doctor and filed. The vital signs (temperature, pulse and respiration) and blood pressure were checked and recorded. Intravenous infusion of Ringer’s lactate 500ml was given prior to the surgery.
All questions were answered promptly except those beyond the nurse but were answered by the surgeon.
SPIRITUAL PREPARATION
A short prayer for God’s protection throughout the operation was said by the brother of the client before client was sent to the theatre.
SOCIO-ECONOMIC PREPARATION
Client and family were told of the hospital bills, which are surgery fee, daily cost and the medication involved. Drugs that were covered by the National Health Insurance were collected from the hospital pharmacy
INTRA-OPERATIVE
Client had appendicectomy done by a team of doctors and anaesthetist at the Methodist Hospital, Wenchi in the Main theatre at about 10: 32am. He was given both spinal and general anaesthesia because the spinal anaesthesia did not have effect on him even when it was topped up.  The patient monitor was connected with electrodes to check client’s progress as surgery was underway. The abdomen was incised with a diathermy and then a scapel blade with the help of an assisting doctor. The appendix was removed and then sutured. After the surgery client was sent to the recovery ward for further monitoring.
IMMEDIATE POST-OPERATIVE CARE
Client was sent to the recovery ward at about 11:50am in a semi-conscious state with IV Ringer’s lactate in place and dripping well. Client was warmly welcomed and put in a post-operative bed in a recumbent position with head turned to one side to enhance drainage of secretions from the mouth. Side rails were raised to protect client from injury.

chapter: Chapter Four: 4.0 Implementing Patient/Family Care Strategies
heading: 4.2 PREPARATION OF PATIENT/ FAMILY FOR DISCHARGE AND REHABILITATION
text:
4.2 PREPARATION OF PATIENT/ FAMILY FOR DISCHARGE AND      REHABILITATION
Preparation of patient and family is the health education that is given to help maintain and promote good health and prevent possible complications of the disease condition as well as the occurrence of other or similar diseases.
The preparation started from the day of admission through till discharge. On admission client and his family were reassured and informed that, admission may be a short period as recovery time is usually not more than a week on the ward.
 They were educated upon discharge; client should increase his daily fluid intake, eat enough fruits to help in faster healing of the wound, examples Oranges, water melon, and also take in less refined carbohydrates. He was made to understand that once the surgery was performed, the disease condition will not occur again. Client was also advised not to touch the wound with his bare hand since it can lead to infection of the wound.
The need to attend regular check-ups to maintain his health status was also explained to client and relatives. They were reminded of the regular review after discharge, he was told of the review dates. He was also made to know that although he has been given review dates, he can report to the hospital when not well even before the review date. They were informed on the fact that client will be discharged on medication and the need to observe and ensure he takes his drugs regularly at the correct time and right dosage. Client and his brother were also advised on the importance of reporting to the hospital and avoiding over the counter drugs when sick.
Since the hospital bills had being settled by the client and receipts issued, I collected clients prescribed drugs to be taken home and explained how the drugs should be taken, client’s belongings were packed and handed over to the brother to cross check, they were reminded of the review date which was 7th November, 2016. I saw them off to the car park and then bid them good bye.

chapter: Chapter Four: 4.0 Implementing Patient/Family Care Strategies
heading: 4.3 HOME VISITS/FOLLOW UPS/CONTINUITY OF CARE
text:
4.3 HOME VISITS/FOLLOW UPS/CONTINUITY OF CARE
Home visiting is the visit made to clients in their homes to prevent illness and disability, to promote and maintain health, encourage individuals and family to live a healthy life and improve their health status.
FIRST HOME VISIT   (23rd October, 2016)
This visit was scheduled and made in the company of client’s brother on 23rd October, 2016 at 11:30pm while patient was on admission. The purpose of this visit was to familiarize myself with the home and environment of my client in order to know some of the health problem of the area.
Client and brother live in a 2 bed room apartment house roofed with roofing sheets, electricity supply and pipe born water. The kitchen and bathroom were detached from the main building.
I observed that the surroundings were clean with covered drains. They dispose refuse at a container with lid provided by Wenchi Municipal Assembly situated quite a distant away from client’s house.
Family members were commended and educated on the need to maintain a clean environment to prevent diseases from occurring. They were reassured that Client’s condition was progressing and will soon join them in good health. I promised them of another home visit, and asked permission to take leave of them at 1:00pm.
SECOND HOME VISIT (25th October, 2016)
This home visit to my client’s house was unannounced. This was done to observe client and family in their natural state and further assess and evaluate client’s health after discharge.
Client and family were met in a state of good health at 4:00pm at home and their surroundings clean and tidy. I enquired of any complaints with client but had none from client. The wound was assessed for signs of infection but I saw no sign of infections.
His drugs were checked to identify if he was taking them correctly. He was encouraged to continue taking his medication and maintain good nutrition and personal hygiene.
He was reminded of the daily wound dressing and review date and its importance which was eleven (11) days away. Client was told to come to the Methodist Hospital, Wenchi for his wound to be dressed and for continuity of care. They were assured of another visit and I ask them permission to take my leave at 5:20pm.


THIRD HOME VISIT (20th November, 2016)
My last visit to the house of my client was arranged by myself and client’s brother who normally rest at home all day on Sunday. Client was found in a good state of health at 12:45pm as she looked cheerful and feeling better and looking very good.
 I was given a warm welcome by client and family. I spent some time with them conversing about issues of health.
After a good time spent with the family I asked to take leave at 2:00pm, I was then seen off by client and his brother.
Client and his brother expressed their appreciation.
DAY OF REVIEW (15th November, 2016)
On the day of review, client was assisted to go for her folder and accompanied to the consulting room. Client complained that his drugs were finished and was served with Tablets Amoxicillin and clavulanate sodium 1g three times daily for three days. He was advised to continue with those drugs and report immediately, any new development if they do arise.
Client was then sent to Ward for the remaining stitches to be removed. The wound was aseptically dressed after the stitches were removed. Client was educated on how to care for the wound at home, good nutrition and personal hygiene. I accompanied him to the taxi rank to board a car. I bid him fare well as the car took off.

chapter: Chapter Five: 5.0 Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Client And Family
heading: Introduction
text: Evaluation involves comparing the client’s health status with set goals and objectives and judging the process towards goal achievement. It is a systematic review of the effectiveness of nursing intervention and determination of patient’s goals achieved

chapter: Chapter Five: 5.0 Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Client And Family
heading: 5.1 STATEMENT OF EVALUATION
text:
5.1 STATEMENT OF EVALUATION
On 20th October, 2016 client was anxious about the unknown outcome of surgery. An objective to relieve him of anxiety within 24hours was set and was fully met as client verbalized a relief of anxiety and Showing cheerful facial expression and being relaxed.
On 21st October,2016 client complained of not having normal sleep pattern due to the surgical incision. An objective set to make client have a normal sleep pattern within 72hours was fully met as client slept for 6-8 hours at night uninterrupted.
On 21st October,2016 client had high risk of infection due to his surgical wound. An objective set to make Client’s wound  heal without infection by first intention was fully met as client having a clean wound,  no signs of infection and  wound heals by first intention.
On 22nd October, 2016 client had an increased temperature of 38.7oC which was due to infection. An objective set to reduce the body temperature within 2hours was set and was fully met as temperature was 37.7oC on the clinical thermometer.
On 23rd October, 2016 client complained of pain at the incision site. An objective set to reduce the pain within 72hours was fully met as client verbalized reduction in pain at the incision site and seen comfortable in bed.

On 24th October, 2016 client was observed to have no knowledge on his condition and an objective set to educate him on the condition within 2hours was fully met as client patient verbalized adequate knowledge on his condition and giving positive answers to questions asked.

text:
5.2 AMENDMENT OF NURSING CARE PLAN FOR PARTIALLY MET OR UNMET OUTCOME CRITERIA
All goals and objectives set for the various nursing diagnosis were fully met, hence there was no amendment to any of the care given.

chapter: Chapter Five: 5.0 Evaluation Of Care Rendered To Client And Family
heading: 5.3 TERMINATION OF CARE
text:
5.3 TERMINATION OF CARE
This is the final interaction between client and the nurse, as the nurse-patient relationship officially comes to an end, some client’s react emotionally either by relapsing or expressing anger and hostility. Other clients express satisfaction and appreciation for the short but warm professional relationship with them.
With client, the termination was done officially on 20th November, 2016 after the third home visit. Client and family expressed their profound gratitude for the professional care rendered to them. Client and his family were educated on proper care to be given to the client at home and I was about to handover client to a community health nurse but he insisted that he wants to go back to Tema so I advised him to report to the nearest hospital or clinic when ill.

chapter: Chapter Six: 6.0 Summary And Conclusion
heading: 6.1 SUMMARY
text:
6.1 SUMMARY
This is a comprehensive care rendered to Mr. A.A., a 30 year old mechanic at Tema who comes from Wenchi in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.
He was admitted to male`s ward of the Methodist Hospital Wenchi from the outpatient department.
Client was diagnosed of acute appendicitis and had appendicectomy done on the                                  21st October, 2016
An urgent blood sample for grouping and cross matching were done prior to the surgery.
the planning and implementation of the care was successful with the cooperation and particularly the participation of the client and family, and the entire staff of male`s ward.
Mr. A.A. was discharged home on the 24th October, 2016.








6.2CONCLUSION
In conclusion, it is obvious that caring for the patient was very challenging but successful. The client and his family benefited from the study as they realized the health needs of client and showed preparedness to take necessary measures to solve them.
The study has equipped me with in-depth knowledge on appendicitis and its surgical treatment. I have been able to practice the nursing process successfully to the best of my ability in the management of the disease condition.
Finally, the patient/family care study has helped me in gaining confidence in rendering selfless and professional care to clients with same disease condition with little or no supervision
I therefore support the idea of patient/family care study as part of the programme to pursue to enhance quality assurance of patient care.
